# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate the existing action bodies and helpers into sibling
  modules, adjust imports and registration wiring; do not refactor their logic,
  rename flags, or reword user-facing output.
- **Entry point is fixed.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` must remain the dynamic
  import target in `src/command-registry.ts`; the split happens *behind* that
  path.
- **CLI-agnostic logic stays put.** `src/doctor/*.ts` holds CLI-independent
  validation logic (`status-stage-check`, `dependency-check`, `file-paths-check`,
  `hook-upgrade`, `foreign-items-check`, `audit-gaps-check`, `parent-check`,
  `podcast-scripts-check`, `fix`). It is consumed as-is; this item does not
  restructure it.
- **Serial, tree-green landing.** Extract the smallest subcommands first and the
  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and
  passes the suite.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the doctor CLI contract, and no
  edits to the TUI or other commands.

## Existing state

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is 1,658 lines on today's `dev`. Inventory of logical
sections (line ranges from the current checkout):

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | File header + imports | 1–30 | 30 |
| 2 | `DAY_MS` constant | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | `formatCacheBytes` helper | 33–46 | 14 |
| 4 | `DoctorOptions` type | 47–50 | 4 |
| 5 | `PendingUpgradeState` + `detectPendingUpgrades` | 51–92 | 42 |
| 6 | `buildPendingUpgradeFinding` | 93–129 | 37 |
| 7 | `printPendingUpgradeNotice` | 130–151 | 22 |
| 8 | `PendingCacheState` + `detectPendingCacheState` | 152–196 | 45 |
| 9 | `printPendingCacheNotice` | 197–207 | 11 |
| 10 | `register()` prologue + root `doctor` command definition | 208–217 | 10 |
| 11 | `doctor upgrade` action | 218–418 | 201 |
| 12 | `doctor stage-sync` action | 420–549 | 130 |
| 13 | `doctor prune` action | 551–649 | 99 |
| 14 | `doctor cache` action | 651–715 | 65 |
| 15 | `doctor foreign-items` action | 717–838 | 122 |
| 16 | `doctor audit-gaps` action | 840–877 | 38 |
| 17 | `doctor dangling-parents` action | 879–948 | 70 |
| 18 | `doctor priority` action | 950–1036 | 87 |
| 19 | `doctor file-paths` action | 1038–1150 | 113 |
| 20 | `doctor migrate` action | 1152–1271 | 120 |
| 21 | Root `doctor` action (findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices) | 1273–1657 | 385 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Single consumer.** Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports the module
  (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`), and only for the default
  export. There is no cross-module use of helpers defined in the file, so
  extraction needs no public barrel beyond the unchanged default export.
- **Existing precedent for a nested sibling directory.** `src/sync.ts` (1,828
  lines, itself the subject of WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ) already sits beside a
  `src/sync/` directory (`src/sync/merge-utils.ts`), so `src/commands/doctor.ts`
  + `src/commands/doctor/` follows an established repository shape.
- **CLI layer vs validation layer.** `src/doctor/` modules are pure,
  `PluginContext`-free validators; the monolith's bulk is CLI registration and
  output rendering. The split therefore belongs in the command layer, not in
  `src/doctor/`.
- **Test surface to keep green (unmodified).** 18 existing doctor suites —
  `tests/doctor-{dependency-check,file-paths,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-check,hook-upgrade,podcast-scripts,retired-stage,status-stage}.test.ts`
  and `tests/cli/doctor-{audit-gaps,cache,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-push,foreign-items,priority,prune,stage-sync,upgrade-notice,upgrade}.test.ts`.
  Source: `ls tests/doctor-*.test.ts tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Reduce `src/commands/doctor.ts` to a thin registrar that wires the root
`doctor` command and delegates each subcommand to its own module under a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory. Starting decomposition (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/doctor.ts` | Registrar only: imports the per-subcommand registrars, registers the root `doctor` command definition, documents the module layout | ~120 |
| `src/commands/doctor/notices.ts` | Shared helpers: `DAY_MS`, `DoctorOptions`, `formatCacheBytes`, pending-upgrade detection/notice, pending-cache detection/notice | ~180 |
| `src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` | `doctor upgrade` (migrations + hook upgrade, dry-run/confirm) | ~205 |
| `src/commands/doctor/stage-sync.ts` | `doctor stage-sync` | ~135 |
| `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` | `doctor prune` | ~105 |
| `src/commands/doctor/cache.ts` | `doctor cache` | ~70 |
| `src/commands/doctor/foreign-items.ts` | `doctor foreign-items` | ~130 |
| `src/commands/doctor/audit-gaps.ts` | `doctor audit-gaps` | ~45 |
| `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` | `doctor dangling-parents` | ~75 |
| `src/commands/doctor/priority.ts` | `doctor priority` | ~95 |
| `src/commands/doctor/file-paths.ts` | `doctor file-paths` | ~120 |
| `src/commands/doctor/migrate.ts` | `doctor migrate` (JSONL → SQLite) | ~125 |
| `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` | Root `doctor` action: findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices | ~390 |
| `tests/doctor-line-count-guard.test.ts` | Additive guard: every doctor module ≤ 1,000 lines (repo convention keeps tests under `tests/`) | ~60 |

Each per-subcommand module exports a single `register<Sub>Command(...)` function
taking the narrow typed context, keeping the extracted action bodies
byte-for-byte faithful apart from their new signature and imports. The registrar
invokes them in the same order as the monolith so `wl doctor --help` output is
unchanged.

Implementation order (each step leaves the tree green): `cache` → `audit-gaps` →
`dangling-parents` → `priority` → `prune` → `file-paths` → `migrate` →
`foreign-items` → `stage-sync` → `upgrade` → root validation/`--fix` → guard
test + docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — reduce to a registrar; keep `export default register(ctx: PluginContext)`.
- `src/commands/doctor/notices.ts` — new; shared notice/formatting helpers moved from the monolith.
- `src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` — new; `doctor upgrade` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/stage-sync.ts` — new; `doctor stage-sync` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — new; `doctor prune` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/cache.ts` — new; `doctor cache` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/foreign-items.ts` — new; `doctor foreign-items` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/audit-gaps.ts` — new; `doctor audit-gaps` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — new; `doctor dangling-parents` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/priority.ts` — new; `doctor priority` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/file-paths.ts` — new; `doctor file-paths` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/migrate.ts` — new; `doctor migrate` action.
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — new; root `doctor` action, findings aggregation and `--fix` prompt.
- `tests/doctor-line-count-guard.test.ts` — new; additive ≤1,000-line guard for the doctor module family (repo convention keeps test files under `tests/`).
- `src/command-registry.ts` — verify unchanged (dynamic import path stays `./commands/doctor.js`).
- `src/doctor/*.ts` — verify unchanged (CLI-agnostic validators, consumed as-is).
- `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`, `tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md` — verify doctor references remain accurate; add a module-layout note where a source-layout note already exists.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class* (parent refactor
  series; this item was created by its intake sweep). Producer decision Q1 → A
  is inherited: each oversized production file gets its own work item, evaluated
  and decomposed where appropriate.
- **WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO** — *Decompose WorklogDatabase god class
  (src/database.ts, 2,584 lines)* (completed). Precedent for the AC pattern:
  unchanged public entry point, unmodified tests, per-module line ceiling, no
  cycles.
- **WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E** — *Refactor guard: downtime-worker split invariants*
  (completed). Precedent for the additive split-guard test adopted in AC6.
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** — *Refactor: decompose src/sync.ts god class* (open).
  Sibling item; `src/sync/` is the directory-shape precedent used here.
- **WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ** — *Refactor: decompose src/commands/init.ts god class*
  (open). Sibling item in the same `src/commands/` directory; shares the
  "registrar + per-subcommand modules" shape.
- **WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J** — *wl doctor prefix: rename the project prefix …*
  (open). A future doctor subcommand that will consume the new module pattern;
  it is **not** in scope here.
- **WL-0MUTVB271007YKJZ**, **WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G**, **WL-0MSALMLYK00604IA**,
  **WL-0MQPS28DW008QFL3** — completed doctor features whose tests form part of
  the unchanged regression gate.
- Documentation: `CLI.md` (doctor command reference), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
  (source layout references), `docs/migrations.md` (`doctor upgrade`/`migrate`
  guidance), `docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` (`doctor file-paths` guidance).

Automated report: `find-related` (`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGKH1770008MNU.md`)
matched the three sibling refactor items WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1
and WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, plus `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
`packages/herdr/README.md` and `CLI.md` as file matches.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Lost provenance / silent logic drift (medium).** Large block moves invite
  opportunistic edits. *Mitigation:* move-only rule (AC3), the unmodified doctor
  test suites as the behaviour gate, and a review that diffs each moved block
  against the original.
- **Registration-order or wiring regression (medium).** Commander renders
  subcommands in registration order, so running registrars in a different order
  reorders `wl doctor --help`, and a forgotten registrar silently drops a
  subcommand. *Mitigation:* AC3 plus a review that diffs root and per-subcommand
  `--help` output against the pre-refactor binary, and the unmodified CLI suites
  (which exercise every subcommand) as the wiring gate.
- **Import cycles through the registrar (low).** A module importing back from
  `src/commands/doctor.ts` would create a cycle. *Mitigation:* AC5 — modules
  import only concrete siblings; the registrar imports downward only.
- **Test-file temptation (low).** Rewriting the 18 doctor suites' import paths is
  the easy path but erases the behaviour-preservation signal. *Mitigation:* AC3
  makes unchanged tests a hard gate.
- **Guard-test scope creep (low).** A line-count guard test could grow into a
  repo-wide lint rule. *Mitigation:* AC6 scopes it to the doctor module family
  only; a repo-wide rule is recorded as a linked follow-up
  (SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD covers the skill-level check).
- **Assumption A1 — single task, not an epic.** The file has 11 naturally
  separated subcommands and no cross-cutting mutable state, and the largest
  extracted module is ~390 lines; a single `task` with a sequenced inner order
  matches the `database.ts` precedent (WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO) rather than the
  epic-per-module shape used for the 9,362-line `downtime-worker.ts`.
- **Assumption A2 — module home is `src/commands/doctor/`.** The extracted code
  is CLI registration and output rendering (needs `program`/`output`/`utils`),
  while `src/doctor/` is deliberately `PluginContext`-free validation logic. The
  `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/` pair establishes the nested-sibling-directory
  shape.
- **Assumption A3 — no producer answer required.** Every open decision here is
  resolvable by repository inspection or inherited from WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7
  decisions; no new scope or contract question is raised.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Restructuring `src/doctor/`, rewording doctor
  output, merging subcommands, and adding a repo-wide file-length lint rule are
  tempting and **out of scope**; each is recorded as a linked follow-up rather
  than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q0 (inherited scope) — Does the "no file > 1,000 lines" goal apply to this
file specifically, or should this item also decompose other oversized files?**

- **Answer (producer, 2026-10-20, via WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 Q1 → A):** *"Create
  refactor work items for each of the other files. … If any file is >1000 lines
  it should be evaluated for refactoring and if appropriate a work item should
  be created."*
- Applied: this item is scoped to `src/commands/doctor.ts` only; siblings have
  their own items (WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, …), and
  SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD carries the skill-level check.
- Source: `wl show WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 --json` description, Appendix Q1.

**Q1 (consumer surface) — Does anything outside `src/commands/doctor.ts` import
symbols from it, i.e. must a compatibility barrel be preserved?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** no. Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports
  the module, and only as `import('./commands/doctor.js')` for the default
  export; no other file imports any helper from it. Preserving the default
  `register` export is therefore sufficient and no re-export barrel is needed.
  Research: `grep -rn "commands/doctor" src/`; `src/command-registry.ts:114`.
- Consequence: AC2 requires only the unchanged default export; internal modules
  may be imported directly by the registrar.

**Q2 (module home) — Should the extracted modules live in `src/doctor/` or a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** `src/commands/doctor/`. The bulk of the
  monolith is CLI registration and output rendering (it needs `program`,
  `output`, `utils`), whereas `src/doctor/` is deliberately
  `PluginContext`-free validation logic (`status-stage-check.ts`,
  `file-paths-check.ts`, …) consumed by the command layer. `src/sync.ts` beside
  `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` establishes the nested-sibling-directory shape.
  Research: `head src/doctor/*.ts` import sections; `ls src/sync/`.
- Consequence: recorded as Assumption A2 and in the Key Files list; `src/doctor/`
  stays untouched.

**Q3 (delivery shape) — One task or an epic decomposed into child items?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection + precedent):** one `task`. The file has 11
  naturally separated subcommands, no module-level mutable state to preserve,
  and the largest extracted module is ~390 lines. `database.ts` (2,584 lines) was
  decomposed as a single task (WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO); the epic-with-children shape
  was adopted for the 9,362-line `downtime-worker.ts` because each extraction
  there was a large, independently mergeable slice.
- Consequence: recorded as Assumption A1; implementation still lands in a
  sequenced, tree-green order (smallest subcommands first, root validation last).

**Q4 (verification of the line ceiling) — How is "no file > 1,000 lines" kept
true after this refactor, given there is no repo-wide file-length lint?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** an additive guard test in the doctor module
  family (AC6), mirroring `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` added by
  WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E. A repo-wide rule is out of scope and is covered by the
  SorraAgents follow-up SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD (evaluate >1,000-line files in the
  refactor skill).
- Consequence: AC6 added; guard test is additive only, so AC3's
  "no existing test modified" still holds.

**Q5 (current size drift) — The item was created against a 1,582-line file; the
file is 1,658 lines today. Does that change scope?**

- **Answer (agent, by inspection):** no scope change. The section inventory above
  was recomputed from today's `dev`; the extra ~76 lines are inside the existing
  `upgrade` and root-validation action bodies, which are already in scope.
  Research: `wc -l src/commands/doctor.ts` → 1,658.

# Herdr downtime dispatch: claim local capacity via proxy reservation (never send-then-hope)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher polls `/llama/local/status` and launches panes into what it believes is free capacity. Two defects remain even after `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing) ships:

1. **Poll-and-send is racy.** With the prefill gate serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), new starts are a single ticket. Two herdr instances polling in the same 10 s tick can both be admitted and launch; the second queues behind the first's prefill and, on the current proxy, times out and goes remote (measured on the proxy side: queue depth reached 7 in-window while `available_slots` still reported 2 with the gate saturated; 261 requests fell back after queueing, 215 after the full 120 s). An idle window can be *observed* by N instances but only *owned* by one.
2. **The sent-work model is wrong for mid-session pressure.** Even with correct pane pacing, pane turns are continuous (29 sessions, median 30 requests/session on 2026-10-21); those turns cannot be gated by idle windows at all. The dispatcher (and the agents it spawns) must be able to claim capacity *per request* and defer when refused.

The proxy is adding an atomic reservation handshake — `POST /llama/local/reserve` returning a gate ticket, or a `429 {reason, retry_after_s}` refusal — plus `X-Local-Preference: local-only` and `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers (llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`). This item consumes that handshake so the dispatcher never launches work it cannot start.

## Goal / users

- As the downtime dispatcher, I want to launch exactly **one pane per idle window** (operator requirement, asserted in the comment on `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`): I ask the proxy for a ticket, launch only with a ticket, and defer with `retry_after` when refused — never poll-then-hope.
- As an agent session spawned by herdr, I want per-turn capacity claims so my turns either get a ticket (local) or an immediate, honest refusal to fall back (remote) — never a silent 120 s proxy-side wait.

## Desired change

1. **Reservation client:** on each dispatch decision, call `POST /llama/local/reserve` (reusing the existing single-flight status poll cadence; no new polling) with the pane's expected token size, priority and cache state.
   - Ticket granted → launch with `X-Local-Reservation` on the first request; treat the ticket as the pane's entry to the gate.
   - Refused (`429`) → defer with `retry_after`, record decision reason (`reserved-fallback` / `prefill-gate` / `queue-full`…).
   - Endpoint absent / failure → fail-open fall back to the `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` polling behaviour (never a hard failure against an older proxy).
2. **One-per-idle-window assertion:** after a successful launch, no second pane is launched until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight < local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** the reservation was granted for that specific launch. Test the two-instances-same-tick race.
3. **Per-turn claims for agent sessions:** the herdr agent runner passes `X-Local-Preference: local-only` for work the operator marks local-first and `remote-ok` for background work; turns then receive the proxy's honest refusal instead of a silent fallback, and the runner records `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` from responses into the decision log.
4. **Decision-log evidence:** each dispatch/defer records ticket state, `admit`, `projected_wait_s`, `retry_after_s`, and the response route headers.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — reserve client:** when the proxy serves the reserve endpoint (fixture), a dispatch first receives a ticket and only then launches with the reservation header; a refused ticket defers with `retry_after` and is recorded (`downtime-worker.mock.test.ts`-style mocked fetch, following the existing fixture pattern).
- **AC2 — failure mode backcompat:** endpoint absent/500/timeout → exactly today's polling behaviour, no crash, no stuck pane (tests for each).
- **AC3 — one-per-idle-window:** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
- **AC4 — per-turn preference:** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
- **AC5 — docs:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the reservation handshake, the one-per-idle-window rule, and the preference policy knob (with matching code comments).
- **AC6 — suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single-flight status poll; the reservation call may piggyback on the same request cadence (no new polling loops).
- Fail-open: an older proxy is fully supported — absent fields/endpoint never block dispatch.
- Pacing only reduces concurrency; never raise the free-slot budget, never bypass fail-closed per-slot handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Keep it surgical: this item extends `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`'s pacing with the atomic claim; it does not rewrite the dispatcher.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reserve call, ticket header, deferral on refusal.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` / `.idle.test.ts` / `.test.ts` / `.fixtures.ts` — reserve + race tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/` agent-runner request path — `X-Local-Preference`, route-header parsing, decision log.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Related work

- **Depends on:** llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (proxy reservation endpoint + headers); adopts the contract it ACs.
- **Extends:** `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing — poll-based); its comment asserts the one-per-idle-window requirement.
- **Siblings:** `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` (per-slot capacity, completed/in_review), `WL-0MVHSZR9C0012NQY` (idle-age signal), `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` (fail-closed per-slot availability).
- **Proxy-side quad:** `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware guard, prerequisite), `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (reservation, this item's dependency), `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (queue sweep after reservations).

## Risks

- **Reservation latency:** an extra round trip per dispatch. Mitigation: piggyback on the status poll cadence and measure; the ticket TTL covers the launch.
- **Over-deferral:** a pessimistic proxy refusal could starve panes. Mitigation: refusals only on calibrated verdicts (proxy fail-open) and the client-side fail-open path.
- **Contract drift:** the proxy contract is new; version the request (additive fields) and keep the fail-open parsing strict-but-tolerant.

# `wl sync` perf — a no-change sync must not re-import and re-index the whole store

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) profiled `wl sync` on a 123.7 MB F1 fixture (2,600
items / 26,000 comments / 259 dependency edges, 78.5 MB JSONL) against a local
bare remote with the built (`dist`) CLI. Measured breakdown:

| Phase | Measured |
|---|---|
| CLI start-up (`wl --version`) | 0.23–0.37 s, 59 MB RSS |
| Pull: fetch + `git show` + JSONL parse + merge (`wl sync --dry-run`) | 3.39 s wall, 498 MB peak RSS |
| Persist: `db.import(items + edges + audits)` | **14.0 s** |
| Persist: `db.importComments(26,000)` | **43.5 s** (114.9 s with the host loaded) |
| Export: full JSONL (78.5 MB) | 2.37 s wall, 538 MB peak RSS |
| Git push to a LOCAL bare remote (fetch 0.06 s, `git show` 0.65 s, worktree add 0.90 s, `git add` 0.93 s, worktree remove 0.06 s) | ≈ 3 s |
| Whole `WL_DELTA_EXPORT_DISABLED=1 wl sync` | 91.8 s / 194.4 s wall under host load; 918–920 MB peak RSS |

CPU profiles of the persist phase (`node --cpu-prof`, self time):
`db.import` = 77.9 % `upsertFtsEntry` + 10.3 % `clearWorkItems`;
`db.importComments` = 90.2 % `upsertFtsEntry` (then 2.7 % `saveComment`,
2.6 % `clearComments`).

The sync re-imports every item and every comment and then re-indexes the FTS
row of EVERY item, even when the merge result is unchanged — so a zero-change
sync pays the whole cost. This is the largest measured cost driver in the
worklog tooling, and it is deliberately NOT absorbed by the Herdr epic (intake
scope-creep guard): the Herdr refresh never calls `wl sync` synchronously.

## Target outcome

A `wl sync` whose merge result is unchanged performs no per-record rewrite and
no FTS work, and a changed sync indexes only the changed records — with every
merge/watermark/delta semantic unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits). A no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes; a CPU profile of the persist phase shows no `upsertFtsEntry` cost for it.
- Persist-phase time on the 123.7 MB F2 fixture drops to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented F2 commands and quoted in the completion comment.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.
- Phase timings are observable (log lines and/or `--json` fields for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) so the F2 stage harness can reproduce a before/after breakdown with the documented commands.
- Docs updated (`DATA_SYNCING.md` and/or a `docs/dev/` note) with the re-runnable measurement commands and the before/after table.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist phase (`db.import`, `db.importComments`).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertComments()`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — F1 fixture generator and the F2 `runStageProfile` evidence harness.

## Re-runnable evidence (from F2)

```sh
# 1. Generate the full-scale fixture (2,600 items / 26,000 comments / 123.7 MB)
npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts --profile full --stages --json

# 2. Time performSync's persist phases on a DISPOSABLE COPY of the store
#    (never mutates the input; prints JSON with --json)
npx tsx packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts \
  --worklog-dir <fixture>/.worklog --json
```

Representative measured output on the quietest run (2026-10-22T22:30Z,
host load ~3): `sqlite-open` 9 ms, `read-local` 98 ms, `parse-jsonl` 229 ms,
`merge` 222 ms, **`persist-items` 14.9 s**, **`persist-comments` 68.7 s**,
`export-jsonl` 1.79 s → persist = 97 % of the 85.9 s pipeline. A CPU profile
of the persist calls shows 77.9 % (`db.import`) and 90.2 % (`db.importComments`)
of the CPU in `upsertFtsEntry`. Under shared-host load the same phases ranged
to 43.5 s / 163.2 s, so quote the ratio and the CPU profile shares, not a single
wall number.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6): the measured breakdown, host context and
  the decision record live there.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MM79H1JR0ZFY0W2** – wl gh import: no progress feedback during comment fetch phase (completed)
- **WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N** – F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync` (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absorbed, acceptance, add, advance, audits (+157 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, audits, background, bare, baseline (+144 more)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — matched: 0mvjv2nng00771c6, acceptance, add, baseline, blocked (+141 more)

## Plan

Decomposed into four children, test-first and dependency-ordered:

| # | Child | Delivers | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify: persist write-detection regression tests (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) | Default-suite tests pinning zero-write/zero-FTS no-change behaviour and write proportionality | AC1, AC3, AC4 |
| 2 | Impl: change-detection persist in `db.import` / `db.importComments` (WL-0MVK6S9TN00500UL) | Diff-based persist, FTS proportional to changed items, one transaction per record type | AC1, AC3, AC4 |
| 3 | Impl: sync phase-timing observability (WL-0MVK6SD5O001K901) | Per-phase timings for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push | AC5 |
| 4 | Measure and document: persist perf before/after (WL-0MVK6SDU90036BBX) | F2-scale before/after measurement (≤ 10 % target) plus docs | AC2, AC6 |

Dependencies: 1 → 2, 2 → 3, 2 → 4, 3 → 4.

Design decisions recorded for the implementation child:

- `import()` keeps destructive-replace semantics: records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (with their FTS rows), while records whose merged value is unchanged are not re-saved.
- The later-`activityAt` merge is preserved: an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted, so no comment activity timestamp is lost (this never triggers on a true no-change sync).
- `clearWorkItems()` / `clearComments()` keep their current behaviour for `importData()`, `doctor migrate` and `clear()`; the sync path uses targeted FTS-row deletion instead of a full FTS clear.
- Comment change detection is new (no `hasCommentChanged` exists today): compare the persisted comment identity/content fields.
- The delta path (`upsertItems` / `upsertComments`) is in scope for the "never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge" AC: `upsertComments()` looks up only the affected parent ids instead of scanning every item.
- `docs/DATA_SYNCING.md` does not exist in this repository, so the documentation AC is satisfied by a `docs/dev/` note plus an update to F2's `wl sync` persist section.

Vertical slice check: each child is an end-to-end slice — 1 ships tests plus write instrumentation, 2 ships the rewritten persist path with the suite green, 3 ships instrumentation plus its regression test, 4 ships the measurement and docs. No horizontal-only phases.

Between phases: re-read the next child's description (and any comments on this item) before starting it; the persist diff design in child 2 determines the exact phase boundaries measured in child 4.

Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-23 — plan session decomposed this item into 4 children (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO, WL-0MVK6S9TN00500UL, WL-0MVK6SD5O001K901, WL-0MVK6SDU90036BBX), wired 4 dependency edges, and reflowed the acceptance-criteria bullets to one line each so machine AC-coverage extraction reads each full criterion.

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

## Summary

`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` in this repo has no `syncAllowedAuthors` list, so `wl sync` runs the author-identity gate in strict mode: it refuses to merge any incoming commit on `refs/worklog/data` whose author email differs from the store's `git config user.email`. The shared ref carries 3,687 commits authored by `pi@local` while this checkout's `user.email` is `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, so agent-initiated `wl sync` runs here were refused and needed `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Fix (as shipped)

Declare a narrow allow-list in `.worklog/config.yaml` — **not** in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`: that file is this repository's project *template* (`projectName: TestProject`, `prefix: TEST`), so identities listed there would leak into every project created from it.

```yaml
syncAllowedAuthors:
  - 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
  - pi@local
```

Never use `null`/`true` (allow-all); empty-author commits must stay refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The effective `syncAllowedAuthors` (defaults merged with `.worklog/config.yaml`) lists both identities, and `config.yaml` never shadows a defaults entry with a narrower list.
- [x] `wl sync` and `wl sync --dry-run` succeed in this checkout without `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [x] A guard test drives the real config merge and the real gate: listed authors accepted, unknown author refused, empty author refused even with the allow-all override (`tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`).
- [x] Full project test suite passes with the new changes — re-verified at HEAD `d688a370` on 2026-10-27 (`run_tests.py --scope full`: 283 files / 4131 tests, 0 failures). The earlier blocker `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts` was fixed and closed via `WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0` (commit `40143a30`).

## Observed

Found while filing WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J (prefix rename request) on 2026-10-24; the first sync was completed with `--allow-foreign-author` as a one-off, then `git pull` was run and `wl sync` re-tested.

## Notes (verification session 2026-10-27)

Implementation commit `6c598200` was already on `dev`; this session verified all ACs against HEAD `d688a370` and closed the lifecycle. Effort: Small; Risk: Low (effort-and-risk estimates persisted).

# If Critical item is a child it should not show in top level herdr selection list (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist renders critical-priority work items that have a `parentId` at the **top level** of the selection list, even when their parent is also listed — so a critical child appears twice: once as a standalone top-level row and once under its parent when expanded. The top level should contain only root items; a critical child must appear only as a child.

Confirmed live reproduction: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`, parent `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`) is a child of `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (critical, in-progress). Both render at top level.

## Users

- **Producer / operator using the Herdr worklist** — browses the top-level selection list to choose what to work on next.
  - *As a producer, I want the top-level list to contain only root work items, so I am not shown the same unit of work twice and the list stays short enough to scan.*
- **Developer/agent triaging critical work** — needs release-blocking critical work to remain discoverable.
  - *As a triager, I want a critical child to be reachable from the top level via its parent, so hiding the duplicate row does not make the work invisible.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Top-level invariant**: the default Herdr worklist contains **no** item with a non-empty `parentId`, critical items included. Enforced on the merged set (browse feed + all mandatory subsets) for **both** fetch paths — the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle path (`assembleDefaultWorklist`) and the per-subset fallback — and by removing the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` exception from the root filter in `selectWorkItems`.
2. **Parent substitution preserves reachability**: when a critical child is dropped from the top level, its **root ancestor** (walking the `parentId` chain to the top-most non-child item) is included instead whenever that root is not already in the selected set. The substituted root joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`) and is sorted by its own priority/group. No badge, marker, or indicator is added to the substituted row.
3. **No regression for existing behaviour**:
   - non-critical children remain hidden from the top level exactly as today;
   - drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children);
   - stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with **no** synthetic/substituted rows;
   - the CLI is unchanged for other consumers: `wl list --priority critical` still returns children (the ship critical-items gate must keep seeing them) and `wl worklist`'s `critical` subset keeps its current all-parent-levels query.
4. **Testing & validation**: unit tests cover the removed critical exception, the substitution rule (root ancestor promotion, parent already visible → no duplicate, parent in a non-critical group, count/mandatory interaction), and both fetch paths; the previously added critical-exception tests are updated/inverted. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
5. **Documentation**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. At minimum: the root-filter comment in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, the critical-subset note in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/worklist.ts`, and the Herdr worklist section of `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **No new hot-path `wl` spawn.** Root-ancestor resolution must use the existing in-process SQLite fast path first (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`), with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback. The refresh-spawn budget work (WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) must not regress.
- **No data mutation.** Substitution is display-layer only: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage`.
- **Keep the `wl worklist` critical subset query as-is** (all parent levels, one spawn). It doubles as the discovery feed that tells the Herdr layer which parents to surface; making it root-only would require a second query per refresh.
- **Ship-gate semantics untouched.** `wl list --priority critical --status open` (exit code 7 gate) and the downtime critical candidate path keep their current child-inclusive behaviour.
- Fail-open: if a parent cannot be resolved (missing/deleted), the child is simply not shown at top level — never crash the refresh, never fall back to rendering the child at top level.

## Existing state

- **Why the duplicate exists today.** Commit `cae8ea8a` ("fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list") deliberately reintroduced critical children into the top level: the critical subset query dropped `--root-only` and `selectWorkItems` gained the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception. Rationale: child criticals (e.g. untriaged `[test-failure]` items) were invisible in the worklist while the ship critical-items gate still blocked release on them (exit code 7).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` root filter: `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId || i.priority === 'critical')`; `isMandatoryItem` treats any critical item as mandatory.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — `WORKLIST_LIST_SUBSET_QUERIES.critical = { priority: 'critical', status: ['open','in-progress','blocked','completed'] }` with **no** `rootOnly`, documented as "all parent levels: a critical child is as urgent as a critical root". `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots` are all `rootOnly: true`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchMandatorySubsets` issues `wl list --priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (no `--root-only`); `assembleDefaultWorklist` merges bundle subsets with the browse feed then calls `selectWorkItems` + `regroupWorkItems`; the per-subset fallback mirrors this. `fetchItemsByStage` / `fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`.
- `wl worklist` is consumed only by `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (verified by search), so its payload shape is effectively a Herdr-internal contract.
- Current data: 174 critical items, 78 of them children — 77 of those are themselves `completed`/`done` (already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule in `selectWorkItems`), leaving **one** live duplicate: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension has no critical-subset or smart-selection code (removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so no Pi-side change is needed.
- Parent rows already carry `childCount` (rendered as a `Children: N` metadata row and an expand icon), so a substituted parent is discoverable as a container.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`** — root filter becomes `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId)` (no critical exception). Update the doc comment to state the invariant and the substitution contract.
2. **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — add a display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback:
   - partition the critical subset into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level);
   - for each critical child, resolve its root ancestor by walking `parentId` upward;
   - for each resolved root not already present in the merged candidate set, add it to the **mandatory** set (so `browseItemCount` cannot cut it) before `selectWorkItems` runs;
   - resolve parents in-process first (`db.get` via the refresh scope / `withInProcessDb`), falling back to `wl show`; unresolvable parents are skipped (fail-open).
3. **`src/commands/worklist.ts`** — documentation-only update: state that the `critical` subset is intentionally all-parent-levels (discovery feed) and that the top-level-only invariant is enforced by the Herdr consumer.
4. **Tests** — invert/extend `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` (child critical hidden; non-critical children still hidden) and add fetcher-level coverage for both paths in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` plus the per-subset fallback tests.
5. **Docs** — update `packages/herdr/README.md` (worklist/selection behaviour) and the affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — remove the critical exception from the root filter; document the invariant and substitution contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `assembleDefaultWorklist` + per-subset fallback: critical-child partition, root-ancestor resolution, mandatory-set injection; in-process-first parent lookup with `wl show` fail-open fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — invert the "shows child critical items at the top level" case; keep/extend non-critical child cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — bundle path: child critical not rendered at top level; parent substituted and mandatory.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` (per-subset fallback coverage, whichever file currently exercises `fetchNextItems` without the bundle) — same assertions on the fallback path.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — comment/documentation update for the `critical` subset (no behaviour change).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — selection-list behaviour documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — *Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr)* (completed). Introduced the root-only invariant; its critical-related behaviour was later superseded by commit `cae8ea8a`. This item restores the invariant for critical items while keeping reachability via parent substitution.
- **commit `cae8ea8a`** — "fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list" (no work-item reference in the commit message): the deliberate exception this item reverses. Its motivation — critical children flagged by the ship gate being invisible — is preserved through AC2.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — *wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually* (completed): precedent for "represented by parent".
- **WL-0MQI1SX4W0018V9O** — *Child work items appear in Pi TUI selection list when they should be hidden (represented by parent)* (completed): same precedent, Pi side.
- **WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B** — *Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount* (completed): defines the mandatory subsets whose "always shown" rule AC2 preserves for substituted parents.
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** — *Bubble up critical items* (completed): created the dedicated "Critical" group that sits first in the grouped output. Relevant because a substituted parent is **not** critical by priority, so it will not land in that group (see Risks).
- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR** — *Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced* (completed): related priority-inheritance behaviour for critical children.
- **WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE** — mandatory in-progress-root and blocked-root subsets: the sibling subsets that already use `--root-only`.
- **WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** — spawn-budget work governing the consolidated `wl worklist` read and in-process refresh scope that the substitution must reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost top-level visibility (accepted, mitigated).** Hiding critical children means an operator scanning only the top level no longer sees them directly; the ship critical-items gate can still block a release on a child. Mitigation: AC2 surfaces the root ancestor so the work stays reachable; the parent must be expanded to see the child itself.
- **Substituted parent is not marked critical** (operator decision Q3 = no indicator). It joins the mandatory set and is sorted by its own priority/group, so it may sit in a non-critical section. Risk: the release-blocking signal is less prominent. Accepted; revisit as a separate item if it proves insufficient.
- **Parent resolution cost.** Only critical children trigger a lookup, and only when the root is absent from the merged set (currently one such item). In-process read first; `wl show` is the rare fallback. A per-refresh memo should avoid repeat lookups within a tick.
- **Ancestor promotion depth.** A critical grandchild promotes its **top-most** ancestor, keeping the "no child at top level" invariant. Assumption: promoting the root (not the immediate parent) is correct because the top level may only contain roots.
- **Stage/priority-filtered views are exempt from substitution.** They are explicit filters ("every open item in this stage") and already root-only; injecting a synthetic parent row would misrepresent the filter. Accepted assumption: the ship-gate reachability requirement applies to the default worklist.
- **`wl worklist` payload keeps children in the `critical` subset.** Documented as the discovery feed; a future consumer reading the payload directly would still see children. Accepted, documented in `src/commands/worklist.ts`.
- **Scope creep.** No changes to grouping rules, detail views, badges, or the Pi TUI. Any follow-up (e.g. a critical-child indicator on parents) becomes a separate work item.
- **Assumption**: `parentId` is always present in the payloads used (`wl list`, `wl next`, `wl worklist`) — already relied upon by the existing root-only filters.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** – Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (completed)
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** – Bubble up critical items (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed) — *keyword-only match, unrelated*

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: another, appear, child, children, critical, extension, herdr, level, list, selection, should, show, they, top
- `CLI.md` — matched: same keywords
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: same keywords

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (intake round 1): "What should happen to a critical child whose parent is *not* otherwise in the top-level list (e.g. parent is `done`, or filtered out by the current stage/priority view)? (a) hide it entirely, (b) substitute the parent — show the parent row instead, (c) fallback exception — hide when the parent is visible, show the child when the parent is not, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. B"** — substitute the parent; the child is never rendered at top level.
- **Q2** (intake round 1): "Which lists should the fix cover? (a) default Herdr worklist only, (b) all Herdr top-level lists — default worklist, stage-filtered, priority-filtered, plus both fetch paths, (c) (b) plus CLI semantics, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. B"** — all Herdr top-level lists and both fetch paths; CLI `wl list`/ship-gate semantics unchanged.
- **Q3** (intake round 1): "Should a parent row show a 'critical child' indicator (badge/count) when it is surfaced because of a critical child?" — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "3. no"** — no indicator.
- **Derived assumptions (no question asked)**: (i) a critical child promotes its **top-most** ancestor, because the top level may only contain roots; (ii) stage/priority-filtered views get no substitution — they are explicit filters and already root-only; (iii) the substituted parent keeps its own priority/group (no critical marking, per Q3); (iv) an unresolvable parent means the child is simply not shown (fail-open).
- **Research note**: verified via `wl worklist --json` that the `critical` subset is the only mandatory subset without `rootOnly` (174 items, 78 children; 77 of those are `completed`/`done` and already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule, leaving one live duplicate `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` under `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`). Traced the deliberate exception to commit `cae8ea8a` (no work-item reference) which removed `--root-only` from the critical query and added the `priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception to keep ship-gate-flagged child criticals visible. Confirmed `wl worklist` has a single consumer (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) and that `fetchItemsByStage`/`fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`. Confirmed the Pi TUI has no critical-subset/smart-selection code.

# Default downtime local preference should be remote-ok

**Headline:** Flip the downtime locality default from `local-only` to `remote-ok`
so unattended downtime work never queues the local slot the operator may need,
while `local-only` remains an explicit per-deployment opt-in.

## Problem statement

Downtime-dispatched panes default to `local-only`, so on a contended local slot
the proxy refuses the request immediately instead of falling back: the
unattended work simply does not run, even though remote capacity is available.
`local-only` is only *safe* when the operator has deliberately said "this work
must run here" — as a blanket default it strands work that could have run
remotely, and (see WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G) cannot serve prompts above the local
provider's context ceiling at all.

## Users

- **Producer/operator running downtime dispatch.** Wants backlog work to keep
  moving unattended without competing for the local slot they need for
  interactive work.
- **Operator of a deliberately local-first deployment.** Wants the current
  fail-fast-local behaviour preserved, selected explicitly rather than by
  default.
- **Operator auditing dispatch behaviour.** Wants the route log to show
  `preference: remote-ok` on a default deployment, so "which default applied?"
  is evidence, not guesswork.

User stories:

- As a producer, I want downtime-dispatched panes to default to `remote-ok` so a
  contended local slot does not silently stall my backlog.
- As a producer running a local-first box, I want `downtimeLocalPreference:
  local-only` to keep today's behaviour exactly, with no other switch needed.
- As an operator, I want the route log of an unconfigured deployment to record
  `remote-ok`, so I can confirm the new default is live after deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Default constant.** `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` is `'remote-ok'` in
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`; the module header documents
  `remote-ok` as the default and `local-only` as the per-deployment opt-in,
  cross-referencing this item and the superseded default in
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ.
- [ ] **Clamp.** `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` resolves every absent/invalid
  input (`undefined`, `null`, `''`, `'auto'`, `'both'`, `'Local-Only'`,
  `' remote-ok'`, `42`) to `remote-ok` via the constant, still passes
  `local-only` / `remote-ok` through verbatim, and never invents a value.
- [ ] **Settings default.** `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference` is
  `'remote-ok'`, and `loadSettings` resolves a missing file, a file without the
  key, and an out-of-alphabet persisted value to `remote-ok`;
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` (default + clamp cases) and
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` are updated to pin it.
- [ ] **Dispatch paths inherit the default.** With no `downtimeLocalPreference`
  in `settings.json`, downtime backlog dispatch, own-backlog fallback,
  audit-batch continuation and scheduled-prompt dispatch all forward
  `remote-ok` to the pane (`--local-preference remote-ok` and
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=remote-ok`), asserted by regression tests; the
  Worklog pi extension route-log test records `preference: "remote-ok"` for a
  `remote-ok` pane so the observable route log matches.
- [ ] **`local-only` stays selectable.** With `downtimeLocalPreference:
  'local-only'` persisted, every dispatch path still forwards `local-only`
  (existing C4-AC1 forwarding tests stay green) and nothing overrides it.
- [ ] **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list + per-turn local preference section)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (where its prose implies a default)
  state `remote-ok` as the default, `local-only` as the opt-in, and make the
  scheduled/background inheritance explicit; related code comments in
  `settings.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts` and `local-preference.ts` are updated.
- [ ] **Testing/validation gate.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit and
  the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` (no ad-hoc test runs).

## Constraints

- **Wire contract unchanged.** The request header alphabet stays exactly
  `local-only | remote-ok`; no new header, value or proxy (LP) change is in
  scope.
- **Fail-open preserved.** Unset/empty/invalid input still resolves to the
  default (now `remote-ok`), never throws and never invents a preference.
- **Optional internal field semantics unchanged.** `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()
  .localPreference` stays optional: absent still means "no `--local-preference`,
  no `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`, no route-log line" (byte-identical launch for
  hand-built/legacy configs). The new default reaches production panes through
  `loadSettings()` → plugin `config()`, which always supplies a value.
- **`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` stays separate** (`remote-ok`) and remains the
  fallback for callers that supply no knob. Scheduled prompts continue to take
  the knob when present — so an explicit `local-only` deployment also makes
  scheduled work local-only. That inheritance must be documented, not silently
  changed.
- **No priority-based rule here.** Priority → preference mapping is
  WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX and layers on top of this default.
- **Interactive panes untouched.** No env var unless the operator exports
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`; no new polling or logging behaviour.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`: `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE =
  'local-only'`, `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`;
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference()` returns `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for
  anything not in the two-value alphabet.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`: `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference`
  uses the constant; `loadSettings()` clamps the persisted value through
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference`, so absent/invalid already follows the
  constant (only the constant needs to change for AC1–AC3 to hold).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` forwards `s.downtimeLocalPreference` into the
  worker config and `s.downtimeLocalPreference`/`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`
  into the headless dispatcher.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` threads `localPreference` through
  `runDispatchTick` → `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchClaimedTier` →
  `spawnAgentPane` → `buildDowntimePaneArgs` (`--local-preference`) and
  `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`); the scheduled-prompt
  path uses `opts.localPreference ?? BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- Tests currently pinning the old default: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`
  (`DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE === 'local-only'`) and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`
  (default and invalid-value clamp cases). Forwarding tests
  (`downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`,
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`) pass explicit
  values and should stay green.
- Documentation currently stating the default: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  (Policy knob paragraph), `packages/herdr/README.md` (setting list and the
  per-turn local preference section), `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`
  (policy-knob cross-reference).

## Desired change

1. Flip `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` to `'remote-ok'` and rewrite the module
   header + clamp doc comments so `local-only` reads as the explicit opt-in.
2. Update the `settings.ts` property comment and default wiring prose.
3. Update/add tests: new default (module + settings), absent-key and
   invalid-value clamping, unchanged verbatim pass-through, dispatch-path
   inheritance with no setting present, and the extension route-log
   `remote-ok` case.
4. Update the three documentation surfaces so the prose matches the code,
   including the explicit-`local-only` scheduled-prompt inheritance.
5. Record the supersession of the pinned C4-AC1 default on
   WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (comment) so the changed decision is auditable.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — flip the default constant and
  rewrite the policy doc comments (default vs opt-in, supersession note).
- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` — pin `remote-ok` as the
  downtime default; keep clamp tests expressed relative to the constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — update the `downtimeLocalPreference`
  property comment; default already derives from the constant.
- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — new default expectation and invalid-value
  clamp expectations (`'auto'`, `42` → `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — comment prose for the
  `localPreference` field and dispatch paths (default now `remote-ok`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — dispatch-path
  inheritance coverage (scheduled prompt, own-backlog fallback, audit-batch
  continuation) with no setting present.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` —
  route-log line with `preference: 'remote-ok'` (and header injection already
  covered for both values).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Policy knob paragraph (default, opt-in,
  scheduled inheritance).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — setting list entry and the per-turn local
  preference section.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — policy-knob prose if it implies a
  local-only default.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** (completed, *Per-turn local preference and route
  logging*) — introduced the knob, the wire contract and the `local-only`
  downtime default (C4-AC1) that this item supersedes; its default-pinning
  tests are updated here.
- **WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8** (completed) — parent downtime-dispatch epic whose
  AC4 slice C4 defined the locality policy.
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** (*Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only
  preference*) — layers priority → preference on top of this default; its
  "explicit operator setting always overrides" rule stays intact.
- **WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G** (*local-only requests over the local provider context
  limits are unprocessable*) — the context-ceiling limitation that makes a
  blanket `local-only` default unattractive; separate scope.
- **WL-0MVNUMI1B0021IGI** (open test-failure, `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`)
  — unrelated failure in the same package; expect possible slot contention when
  running the herdr suites, not a dependency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — cost/route shift.** `remote-ok` lets contended downtime work leave the
  box for a remote (possibly metered) provider. That is the intended trade
  ("never queue local capacity"), but it is a real change in spend profile;
  `local-only` stays the one-line opt-in and the route log makes the route
  visible. Document it, do not hide it.
- **Risk — silently superseding a pinned AC.** C4-AC1 (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ)
  explicitly pinned `local-only`. Mitigation: the brief records the
  supersession, the code comment names it, and a comment is added to the
  predecessor item.
- **Risk — implicit-default migration.** Deployments that never wrote
  `downtimeLocalPreference` start going remote on contention. Intended, but it
  must be called out in the docs (and the release note handled by `/skill:ship`).
- **Risk — hidden default assumptions in tests.** Only
  `local-preference.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` were found
  asserting the old default; the changed-scope gate should confirm nothing else
  depends on it.
- **Assumption.** No proxy/LP change is required: the wire alphabet and headers
  are unchanged, only which value herdr prefers by default.
- **Assumption.** No settings migration is written: an explicit
  `'local-only'` value keeps working verbatim; only absent/invalid input
  resolves to the new default.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Priority-aware preference, context-ceiling routing and
  any "auto" heuristic stay in WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX / WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G — not
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the seed context (goal, exact file,
AC list and related items) was sufficient to draft this brief. Decisions that
would otherwise have been questions were resolved from repo evidence:

- Q: "Does `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` need a separate change, or does it
  follow the constant?" — Answer (research): follows the constant — it returns
  `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` for anything not in the alphabet
  (`packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts`), so the single constant flip makes
  absent/invalid resolve to `remote-ok`. Source: repo inspection. Recorded as
  AC2 to keep the fail-open behaviour explicit.
- Q: "Do scheduled prompts and headless background dispatches need their own
  change?" — Answer (research): no — both already resolve to
  `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` (`'remote-ok'`) when no knob is supplied
  (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchScheduledPrompt`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `spawnBackgroundPi`), and with the new default
  the knob itself is `remote-ok`. Explicit `local-only` deployments inherit the
  knob, which must be documented (Constraint). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Which tests and docs assert the old default?" — Answer (research):
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` and
  `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` assert it; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` describe
  it. Source: `grep` over the main checkout.
- Q: "Does changing the default contradict completed work?" — Answer
  (research): yes — WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ C4-AC1 pinned `local-only`. This item
  supersedes that default; the supersession is recorded here and on the
  predecessor item rather than left implicit. Source: `wl show
  WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX** – Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only preference (open)
- **WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q** – Herdr isIdleStatus: prefer local_active_query over global active_query for idle detection (completed)
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, absent, ac1, ac2 (+345 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, absent, ac1, ac2 (+343 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, ac2, add, added, already (+264 more)
