# Dispatch low-priority work items with local-only preference

**Headline:** Let the dispatch layer derive a pane's locality preference from
the candidate's work-item priority — `low` → `local-only`, everything else →
the deployment default — while an operator who persisted
`downtimeLocalPreference` keeps that value for every dispatch, and record the
resolved preference plus its reason in the dispatch marker.

## Problem statement

Cheap, low-value work should absorb contention on the local slot instead of
competing for remote capacity, while `medium`/`high`/`critical` work keeps the
fail-fast remote route. Today locality is decided per pane from one
deployment-wide knob (`downtimeLocalPreference`, default `remote-ok` since
WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1), even though the candidate's priority is already resolved
at dispatch time and carried through the same plumbing
(`DowntimeCandidate.priority` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` →
`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`). Priority therefore has no influence on the locality
decision it could inform.

## Users

- **Producer/operator running downtime dispatch.** Wants low-priority backlog
  work to stay on the local slot (cheap work absorbs contention) while
  medium/high/critical work is never queued behind it locally.
- **Operator of an explicit locality policy.** Wants `downtimeLocalPreference:
  local-only` (or `remote-ok`) to keep meaning "every downtime pane", with no
  priority-dependent surprises.
- **Operator auditing dispatch behaviour.** Wants the dispatch marker to state
  which preference was used and why (`priority-low` rule vs deployment
  default vs operator setting), so the choice is evidence rather than
  guesswork.

User stories:

- As a producer, I want a `low`-priority item dispatched with
  `local-only` so cheap work uses the local slot and fails fast instead of
  consuming remote capacity.
- As a producer, I want a `high`-priority item dispatched with the deployment
  default (`remote-ok`) so urgent unattended work never stalls on a contended
  local slot.
- As an operator who set `downtimeLocalPreference` explicitly, I want that
  value applied to every downtime pane regardless of item priority.
- As an operator, I want each dispatch marker to record the resolved
  preference and its reason so I can confirm the rule fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Pure resolver.** `resolveDispatchLocalPreference(priority,
  defaultPreference)` is a pure, IO-free function in
  `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` returning `'local-only'` for
  `priority === 'low'` and `defaultPreference` verbatim for every other input
  (`medium`, `high`, `critical`, `undefined`, `null`, `''`, unknown strings),
  unit-tested in `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`.
- [ ] **Precedence.** The dispatch decision is: explicit operator setting
  (persisted, valid `downtimeLocalPreference`) **>** priority rule (**low** →
  `local-only`; everything else → `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`, currently
  `remote-ok`) **>** deployment default. Tests pin all three branches,
  including an explicit `remote-ok` deployment where a `low`-priority dispatch
  still forwards `remote-ok`.
- [ ] **Explicitness detection.** `loadSettings` exposes whether the operator
  persisted the knob (a derived, never-persisted signal: a valid
  `local-only`/`remote-ok` value present in the settings file); absent,
  missing-file and out-of-alphabet values all resolve to "not explicit" so the
  priority rule applies. `defaultSettings.downtimeLocalPreference` stays
  `'remote-ok'` and `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` keeps its two-value
  alphabet (WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 ACs unchanged).
- [ ] **All dispatch paths.** The resolution happens once at the dispatch
  boundary (`dispatchClaimedTier`), so coordination-offer, own-backlog
  fallback, audit-batch continuation, critical-first/normal scan and the
  legacy tier chain all inherit it; scheduled-prompt dispatch (no work item,
  no priority) resolves to the deployment default and records that reason.
  Absent legacy flag/config keeps today's byte-identical forwarding for
  hand-built configs and existing tests.
- [ ] **Marker evidence.** The downtime dispatch marker
  (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) records the resolved
  `localPreference` and a machine-readable `localPreferenceReason`
  (`priority-low` | `default` | `operator-setting`); scheduled-prompt markers
  record theirs too. Marker readers stay backward compatible (unknown/absent
  fields ignored).
- [ ] **Observable route.** Regression tests assert a `low`-priority dispatch
  spawns with `local-only` (`--local-preference local-only` /
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-only`) and a `high`-priority dispatch with the
  deployment default, so the Worklog extension's route log shows the
  corresponding `preference` value.
- [ ] **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and
  `packages/herdr/README.md` state the precedence order (explicit setting >
  priority rule > default), the marker fields and the scheduled-prompt
  behaviour; `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`'s knob cross-reference gains
  the one-line precedence note; related code comments in `local-preference.ts`,
  `settings.ts`, `dispatch-claims.ts` and the worker contract are updated.
- [ ] **Testing/validation gate.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit and
  the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` (no ad-hoc test runs).

## Constraints

- **Wire contract unchanged.** `X-Local-Preference` stays exactly
  `local-only | remote-ok`; no new header, value or proxy (LP) change is in
  scope. The priority rule chooses between the existing two values.
- **Two-value settings alphabet preserved.** `downtimeLocalPreference` keeps
  accepting `local-only | remote-ok` only; explicitness is a *derived*
  property, not a new persisted token (rejected alternative: an `auto` token,
  which would supersede WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1's pinned default/clamp ACs while it
  is still in review).
- **Legacy callers unchanged.** A hand-built `DowntimeWorkerConfig` /
  `dispatchClaimedTier` caller that supplies `localPreference` without the new
  opt-in flag keeps forwarding that value verbatim (byte-identical launch, no
  marker fields added). Only the plugin's `config()` opts a deployment into the
  priority rule, and only when the setting was not persisted.
- **Fail-open preserved.** Resolution never throws and never invents a value:
  unknown priority → deployment default; unknown/absent setting → the
  documented clamp result. The priority lookup is not repeated — the already
  resolved `DowntimeCandidate.priority` is used.
- **Reservation handshake untouched.** `buildLocalReservationRequest` keeps
  `priority: 'background'`; a `local-only` pane still asks for a local ticket
  (the rule changes the per-turn preference, not the admission protocol).
- **Scheduled prompt inheritance unchanged.** Scheduled prompts continue to
  inherit the knob when present and fall back to `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`
  (also `remote-ok`) when the config supplies nothing.
- **Gate-gap awareness.** `tests/herdr/**` and
  `packages/tui/extensions/**/*.test.ts` are outside the configured
  `suiteCommands` (WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR), so new coverage must live in
  `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` to be executed by the `herdr` group; any
  `tests/herdr` edit is documented as such.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — `LocalPreference`,
  `LOCAL_PREFERENCE_ENV_VAR`, `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`,
  `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`,
  `clampDowntimeLocalPreference()`. No priority-aware helper exists.
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` — `mapDowntimeRequestPriority()`
  already maps work-item priority → `X-Priority` (`low` stays `low`,
  `critical` → `high`, unknown → `medium`); priority is therefore available
  and already threaded to the pane, but the locality decision ignores it.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings.downtimeLocalPreference:
  LocalPreference`; `defaultSettings` uses the constant; `loadSettings`
  clamps the persisted value. There is no signal distinguishing "operator
  persisted the key" from "clamped default".
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `config()` passes
  `localPreference: s.downtimeLocalPreference` into the worker config;
  `spawnBackgroundPi` falls back to `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — forwards
  `cfg.localPreference` into both `dispatchFromCoordination` and
  `dispatchDowntimeWork`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — offer path,
  `dispatchFromOwnHead` (own-backlog fallback + audit-batch continuation) and
  the scheduled-prompt stage all forward `opts.localPreference`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` /
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — critical-first / normal scan contexts
  forward `ctx.localPreference` into `dispatchClaimedTier`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` —
  `dispatchClaimedTier` holds the candidate (`priority` available), writes the
  success marker (`recordDispatch`), and forwards `opts.localPreference` to
  `spawnAgentPane`; `dispatchScheduledPrompt` writes its own marker and spawns
  with `opts.localPreference ?? BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` —
  `DowntimeDispatchEvent` carries `itemId`/`kind`/`dispatchedAt`/`stage`/
  `selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`reservationTicketId` (+`GrantedAt`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `DowntimeLogEntry` and the
  marker readers (`dispatchedItemMarkers`, `markerStillExcludes`) ignore
  unknown fields, so new marker fields are backward compatible.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/` — reads
  `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` per request, sets `X-Local-Preference`, writes the
  route log (`preference` field); needs no behavioural change, only its tests
  are the reference for the expected route-log observation.
- Tests already pinning forwarding: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`
  (defaults/clamp), `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` (pane args/env + dispatch
  → spawn thread), `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`
  (scheduled prompt, offer, fallback, continuation forwarding with explicit
  values) and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` (setting default/clamp).

## Desired change

1. Add the pure resolver plus a small reason type to
   `local-preference.ts`, with the module header documenting the precedence
   order and cross-referencing WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 (default) and this item
   (priority rule).
2. Add the derived explicitness signal to `settings.ts` (`PluginSettings` +
   `defaultSettings` + `loadSettings`), documented as derived and
   never-persisted, and keep the persisted alphabet and default unchanged.
3. Plumb the "apply priority rule" opt-in beside `localPreference` through
   `index.ts config()` → worker config → orchestrator → coordination leader /
   dispatch filter → `dispatchClaimedTier` (absent = fixed legacy behaviour).
4. Resolve the preference once in `dispatchClaimedTier` from
   `candidate.priority`, record `localPreference` + `localPreferenceReason` on
   the success marker, and forward the resolved value to `spawnAgentPane`;
   mirror the marker fields for `dispatchScheduledPrompt` (deployment default,
   no priority).
5. Extend `DowntimeDispatchEvent` and `DowntimeLogEntry` with the two optional
   marker fields; keep readers and legacy entries unchanged.
6. Tests: resolver table, precedence branches (explicit `local-only` /
   explicit `remote-ok` with a low-priority candidate / no setting), settings
   explicitness derivation, marker fields for all paths, scheduled-prompt
   marker, and pane forwarding for a low vs high candidate.
7. Documentation: precedence order, marker fields and scheduled-prompt
   behaviour in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and
   `packages/herdr/README.md`; one-line precedence note in
   `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`; code comments updated.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — add
  `resolveDispatchLocalPreference(priority, defaultPreference)` + the reason
  vocabulary; document the precedence order.
- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts` — resolver table (low,
  medium/high/critical, absent/unknown, default passed through verbatim).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — derived `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit`
  in `PluginSettings`/`defaultSettings`/`loadSettings`; property comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `config()` forwards the explicitness opt-in
  beside `localPreference` to the worker.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts` — worker config and
  `spawnAgentPane` docs gain the opt-in flag.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` —
  `dispatchClaimedTier` opts flag + `localPreference` /
  `localPreferenceReason` on `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — resolve once,
  record marker fields, forward the resolved value; scheduled-prompt
  resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` —
  thread the opt-in flag through the existing `localPreference` plumbing.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `DowntimeLogEntry` gains the two
  optional marker fields + docs.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` — dispatch → spawn
  forwarding for low vs medium/high; explicit-setting override.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — offer, own-backlog
  fallback and audit-batch continuation resolve from priority.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — legacy tier chain and
  scheduled-prompt marker/preference.
- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — explicitness derivation cases (outside the
  configured suite commands — see Constraints; mirror any critical case in
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — precedence order, marker fields, route
  log expectation.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — setting description + per-turn section
  precedence.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — one-line precedence cross-reference.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** (completed, *Default downtime local preference should
  be remote-ok*) — flipped `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` to `remote-ok` and
  explicitly excluded the priority rule ("No priority-based rule here …
  layers on top of this default"). This item implements that layer and leaves
  its default/clamp/settings ACs intact.
- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** (completed, *Per-turn local preference and route
  logging*) — introduced the knob, the `X-Local-Preference` wire contract and
  the route log this item's observable evidence relies on.
- **WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8** (completed, *Herdr downtime dispatch: claim local
  capacity via proxy reservation*) — parent epic whose AC4/slice C4 defined the
  locality policy.
- **WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed, *Interactive dispatch request priority*)
  — supplied `DowntimeCandidate.priority` → `X-Priority`, the input this rule
  consumes.
- **WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G** (open, *local-only requests over the local provider
  context limits are unprocessable*) — a `local-only` pane whose prompt exceeds
  the local context ceiling fails; a low-priority item with a large prompt can
  now hit it. Separate scope, watch for interaction.
- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** (open, plan complete, *Canonical test suite excludes
  77 root-level tests/test.ts files*) — the gate gap that leaves
  `tests/herdr/**` unexecuted; drives the test placement constraint.
- **WL-0MVNUMI1B0021IGI** (completed, test-failure) — pre-existing
  `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts` failure in the same package; expect slot
  contention when running the herdr group, not a dependency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — cheap work now fails fast locally.** A `low`-priority pane on a
  contended local slot is refused immediately (by design) instead of waiting
  or going remote, so low-priority backlog can stall while the operator holds
  the slot. That is the intended trade ("absorb contention locally"), and the
  explicit-setting override plus the route log keep it controllable and
  visible.
- **Risk — new derived settings field leaks into `saveSettings`.** The
  explicitness signal must stay derived; persisting it would make every
  explicit deployment permanently explicit after one save. Mitigation: it is
  documented as derived, `saveSettings`/documented JSON omit it, and a test
  writes settings and re-reads the derived value from the presence of the
  persisted knob only.
- **Risk — plumbing churn.** The opt-in flag crosses ~8 files; a missed path
  silently keeps the fixed behaviour. Mitigation: resolve only inside
  `dispatchClaimedTier` (single decision point), and assert each named dispatch
  path (offer / fallback / continuation / scheduled / legacy chain) in tests.
- **Risk — marker/reader compatibility.** New fields must be ignored by
  existing readers; `markerStillExcludes` and `dispatchedItemMarkers` already
  ignore unknown fields, and legacy entries simply omit them.
- **Risk — explicit-`remote-ok` surprise.** Deployments that wrote
  `downtimeLocalPreference: 'remote-ok'` explicitly will *not* get the
  low-priority rule (their setting wins). Documented as the precedence order;
  `wl comment` on WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 is not needed, but the docs must say how
  to opt into the rule (remove the key).
- **Assumption.** Priority comes from the already resolved
  `DowntimeCandidate.priority`; no extra `wl show` lookup is added (no new IO,
  no new timeout).
- **Assumption.** The rule applies uniformly to every downtime kind (audit,
  implement, plan, intake, risk-effort) — it keys on the candidate's priority
  only; a low-priority audit is still low-priority work.
- **Assumption.** Scheduled prompts have no work item and therefore no
  priority; they resolve to the deployment default and record
  `localPreferenceReason: 'default'` (or `operator-setting`).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Context-ceiling handling (WL-0MVNUJG04005QL7G),
  reservation-request priority, a new `auto` settings token, a settings UI and
  any per-kind exemptions stay out of scope — record them as new items if they
  become necessary.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the seed context (goal, proposed
rule, exact ACs and the cross-referenced default-flip item) was sufficient to
draft this brief. Decisions that would otherwise have been questions were
resolved from repo evidence:

- Q: "How can the dispatch layer tell an explicit operator setting from the
  deployment default, when `loadSettings` always returns a clamped value?" —
  Answer (research/design): add a **derived, never-persisted** explicitness
  signal computed in `loadSettings` (true only when the settings file contains
  a valid `local-only`/`remote-ok`), keep the two-value persisted alphabet and
  the `remote-ok` default, and thread a single "apply priority rule" opt-in
  that only the plugin's `config()` sets (when the key is absent). Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (`loadSettings` merge/clamp),
  WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 Constraints ("config() always supplies a value"). The
  rejected alternative — an `auto` settings token — would supersede that
  item's pinned default/clamp ACs while it is still in review.
- Q: "Does the priority rule apply to audit dispatches too?" — Answer
  (research/AC text): yes — the AC keys on "the candidate's priority is low",
  with no kind exemption; audit/implement/plan/intake/risk-effort share the
  same `DowntimeCandidate.priority`. Source: this item's ACs;
  `dispatchClaimedTier` receives the candidate for every kind.
- Q: "What about scheduled prompts, which have no work item?" — Answer
  (research): no priority exists, so they resolve to the deployment default
  (`BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`/knob, both `remote-ok` today) and record
  `localPreferenceReason: 'default'`; an explicit operator setting still wins
  through the same precedence. Source:
  `dispatchScheduledPrompt` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`.
- Q: "Where should resolution happen so all four named paths agree?" — Answer
  (research): at the single dispatch boundary `dispatchClaimedTier`, which
  every path (coordination offer, own-backlog fallback, audit-batch
  continuation, legacy tier chain) funnels through with the candidate in hand.
  Source: `dispatchClaimedTier` call sites in
  `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`.
- Q: "Do existing forwarding tests break?" — Answer (research): no — they pass
  a concrete `localPreference` without the new opt-in, which stays
  "fixed/explicit" behaviour; only the plugin path (absent persisted key) opts
  into the rule. Source: `localPreference` usages in
  `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`,
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`.
- Q: "Should the marker's reason vocabulary include the operator-setting
  case, or only 'priority rule vs default'?" — Answer (design): include it —
  the seed AC asks for the reason so the choice is auditable, and without an
  `operator-setting` value an explicit `remote-ok` deployment would record
  `default`, hiding the fact that the priority rule was bypassed. Source: this
  item's AC text plus the precedence rule in AC2.
- Duplicate check: `wl search` ("priority preference local-only low-priority")
  surfaced only this item and WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, whose brief explicitly
  excludes the priority rule — no overlapping/duplicate item, so this item is
  the distinct implementation of the layered rule.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** – Default downtime local preference should be remote-ok (completed)
- **WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ** – Per-turn local preference and route logging (completed)
- **WL-0MLYHCZCS1FY5I6H** – wl next should not prefer blockers of lower-priority items over higher-priority open items (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mvnuhwh500196k1, absorb, already, always, applies (+86 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvnuhwh500196k1, already, always, applies, audit (+84 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: already, always, applies, audit, available (+67 more)

## Goal

Extract the two remaining narrow relational concerns — comment CRUD and dependency-edge CRUD (including `importData` and the transaction helpers) — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/comments.ts` and `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/edges.ts`.

Fifth vertical slice: modules + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs in one deliverable.

## Scope

- `persistent-store/comments.ts` — `saveComment`, `getComment`, `getAllComments`, `getCommentsForWorkItem`, `deleteComment`, `clearComments`, `rowToComment`.
- `persistent-store/edges.ts` — `saveDependencyEdge`, `deleteDependencyEdge`, `getAllDependencyEdges`, `getDependencyEdgesFrom`, `getDependencyEdgesTo`, `deleteDependencyEdgesForItem`, `clearDependencyEdges`, `importData`, the transaction helpers (`transaction`/`transactionImmediate`), `rowToDependencyEdge`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/comments.ts` contains the comment surface listed in Scope, moved verbatim (same SQL, same `commentsForItem_${workItemId}` cache key, same invalidation), with a responsibility header comment; `rowToComment` moves with it and is not duplicated in the façade.
2. `persistent-store/edges.ts` contains the dependency-edge surface, moved verbatim (same upsert/`ORDER BY`, same `depEdgesFrom_` / `depEdgesTo_` cache keys and invalidation), with a responsibility header comment; `rowToDependencyEdge` moves with it.
3. `importData` is unchanged: same transaction boundary, same delete-then-insert order, same handling of items/comments/edges, same return/void signature, and it composes the item/comment/edge modules rather than re-implementing their SQL.
4. The transaction helpers keep identical semantics (`BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` behaviour, immediate variant, nesting/re-entrancy behaviour as today) and remain reachable from the façade with unchanged visibility.
5. `clearCommentCaches()` remains exported from the class with unchanged name and behaviour, now implemented in `comments.ts`/`cache.ts` rather than inline.
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green; both new modules ≤ 1000 lines.
7. No module under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` imports `./persistent-store.js` — `edges.ts` reaching work-item/comment collaborators must go through the `StoreContext`, never the façade.
8. Move-only: no SQL, ordering, error-message or public-signature change; no existing test file modified.
9. `npm run build:shared` and the changed-scope test gate (test skill) pass — `database.test.ts`, `dirty-tracking.test.ts` and the sync/import suites in particular.
10. `packages/shared/README.md` Package Structure lists `comments.ts` and `edges.ts` with their single responsibilities.

## Minimal implementation

1. Cut the comment methods and their mapper into `comments.ts` as context-taking functions; keep class delegates so signatures are unchanged.
2. Cut the edge methods, `rowToDependencyEdge`, `importData` and the transaction helpers into `edges.ts`; `importData` calls the moved item/comment/edge functions through the context.
3. Keep the existing cache invalidation calls in the same order relative to the write statements — this is where a silent reordering would flip read-after-write behaviour.
4. Re-read the moved blocks against `git show HEAD:packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` to prove no silent edits.

## Constraints

- Move-only; any improvement idea becomes a `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU` item.
- Do not re-implement `importData` on top of higher-level modules in a way that changes its transaction boundary.
- Do not touch `work-items.ts` beyond importing from it.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/comments.ts` — new.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/edges.ts` — new.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/{types,cache,sql-bindings,work-items}.ts` — import sources.
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts`, `.../dirty-tracking.test.ts` — must pass untouched.
- `packages/shared/README.md`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the work-items child (edge/item composition inside `importData` needs the item module in place).

## Deliverables

- Two modules + façade delegation, existing suite untouched and green.
- README entries, commit(s) recorded on this item.

## Goal

Extract audit-result persistence — the audit upsert, waiver/fingerprint reconciliation and the audit read/delete/bulk paths — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/audit-results.ts`.

Sixth vertical slice: module + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs in one deliverable.

## Scope

`persistent-store/audit-results.ts` — `saveAuditResult`, `reconcileAuditInvalidation`, `getAuditResult`, `deleteAuditResult`, `getAllAuditResults`, `saveAuditResults`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/audit-results.ts` contains the full audit-result surface listed in Scope, moved verbatim — same upsert SQL, same fingerprint handling, same `assessAuditInvalidate` / `AuditInvalidationVerdict` usage from `@worklog/shared/icons`, same `parseAuditWaiver` composition, same returned row shape. The file carries a responsibility header comment.

`bumpStateCounter` performs a read-modify-write of the shared counter file. With

detects this as `COUNTER REGRESSION ... last=20 value=19`.

- `tests/unit/read-cache-prune.test.ts` — deterministic regression test for the counter regression + existing cross-process concurrency test.
- `tests/read-cache-prune-child.ts` — cross-process writer/pruner helper used by the concurrency test.

# Leader with no dispatchable items must step down so a peer with work can lead (empty-leader hand-off + peer-offer starvation)

## Problem statement

The fairness rule (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 / WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9) makes leadership
relinquish only on a successful own-backlog dispatch
(`ownBacklogDispatch: true`). When the leader's own backlog is empty AND no
coordination offer is dispatchable, leadership is retained indefinitely — a
peer whose sprint view DOES contain dispatchable work can never win the election.

Compounding: the `no-candidate` cooldown (60-minute full-stop) arms on this
cycle, suppressing all polling including coordination offer scans — starving
peer offers from being dispatched.

Live evidence (2026-10-26): leader `956ca7b9` offered `null` on every
check-in for ~90 minutes, held the machine lease continuously, and at 11:30Z
entered the 60-min cooldown with 2 idle slots while ContextHub's offer
(`WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6`) sat undispached.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants capacity utilised; when the leader is idle, a peer with work
  should become leader and dispatch.
- **Coordinator fleet** — leadership should be a transient role granted to the
  instance with work to do, not permanently held by a no-work instance.
- **Peer offer owners** — their offers should be dispatchable even while the
  current leader is idle.

### User stories

1. *As an operator*, when the leader's own worklog has no dispatchable items,
   I want the leader to release leadership (or trigger a re-election) so an
   instance whose sprint view DOES contain dispatchable work can become leader.
2. *As an operator*, I want the empty-backlog pause path to never suspend the
   dispatch of peer offers — an offer from another root must always be
   dispatchable even while the leader's own root has nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Empty-own-backlog step-down.** In coordination mode, when the leader
   completes a dispatch cycle in which its own head/backlog yields no
   dispatchable candidate (including when the coordination offer scan also
   yielded none), the leader must release leadership (existing
   `releaseLeadership()`, exactly once per cycle) or otherwise trigger a
   re-election, so a peer can win and dispatch from its own sprint view.
   The step-down must be fail-safe (never crash, never double-release) and
   must not fire on cycles that DID dispatch an in-view/offer/own-backlog item.
   **Verification:** unit test — leader with empty own head and no offers
   → `releaseLeadership()` fires exactly once.

2. **No 60-minute peer starvation from an empty own root.** A `no-candidate`
   outcome caused solely by the leader's own empty/gated backlog must NOT arm
   the full-stop cooldown while a peer's coordination entry (or a fresh peer
   check-in) holds a dispatchable item — peer offers remain dispatchable across
   the leader hand-off, and the cooldown (if entered at all) must not suppress
   polling of the offer list.
   **Verification:** unit/integration test — leader root empty, one peer offer
   present → peer offer dispatches or leadership releases within one cycle,
   never a 60-min pause.

3. **Coordination check-in cancels, peer presence cancels.** The existing
   probe-before-pause (WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7) must additionally treat
   "another instance's entry present in the coordination file with a
   dispatchable item" as "not an empty backlog" — vanilla `no-candidate`
   cooldown must not engage merely because the leader's OWN root is empty.
   **Verification:** integration test — empty own root + peer with offer
   → cooldown does NOT arm.

4. **Tests.** Unit/integration coverage: (a) leader with empty own head and
   one peer offer → peer offer dispatches or leadership releases within one
   cycle, never a 60-min pause; (b) leadership release on the empty-own cycle
   fires exactly once and is idempotent; (c) legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`)
   unchanged; (d) existing sprint-view-only contract (WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9) and
   own-backlog-fallback hand-off (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24) regression tests still
   pass.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (leader-election internals).** Implementers may be tempted to
  change `LeaderElectionManager`'s internals (lease TTL, backoff, peer
  discovery). *Mitigation:* only `releaseLeadership()` is called — the election
  primitive is reused, not modified. Any election-behaviour tuning becomes a
  separate work item.
- **Peer-offer dispatch vs. step-down ordering.** Does the peer's offer
  dispatch before or after the step-down? *Assumption:* step-down fires
  unconditionally; whether the offer dispatches in the same cycle or the next
  is implementation-dependent — what matters is that the cooldown never
  suppresses it.
- **Scope creep (cooldown tuning).** Changing `noCandidateCooldownMs` or adding
  a separate "empty-leader" cooldown is tempting but outside scope. Keep the
  existing cooldown and only suppress its arming when peer offers exist.
- **Assumption:** `releaseLeadership()` is idempotent — calling it multiple
  times (double-release) does not crash or corrupt state.
- **Assumption:** the coordination file scan at dispatch time can reliably
  detect peer entries with dispatchable items without a full worklog CLI probe.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing primitives.** `LeaderElectionManager.releaseLeadership()` is
  the sole hand-off mechanism — do not invent a new one.
- **Legacy mode unchanged.** No `coordinationDir` / `leaderManager === null`
  behaviour is unmodified.
- **Step-down only on genuine empty.** Do not fire on cycles that DID dispatch
  an in-view, offer, or own-backlog item.
- **Fail-safe.** Never crash, never double-release; idempotent step-down.
- **One step-down per empty cycle.** The same guard as today: `leaderState =
  false` prevents immediate self re-election.
- **No schema changes.** Coordination-file format, election-file format —
  unchanged.

## Existing state

- `dispatchFromCoordination` (coordination-leader.ts): sets
  `ownBacklogDispatch: true` only when `ownOutcome.dispatched` is true.
- Worker loop (orchestrator-dispatch.ts): calls `releaseLeadership()` only when
  `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true`.
- `no-candidate` path (orchestrator-dispatch.ts:889): probes own root via
  `computeMostImportantItem`; if empty, arms `cooldownUntil` for
  `noCandidateCooldownMs` (default 60 min).
- The probe does NOT scan the coordination offer list — it only checks the
  leader's own root.
- Documented at `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:~186`: "not called when the
  fallback finds nothing — in that case leadership is retained".

## Desired change

- **New step-down trigger:** In coordination mode, when a dispatch cycle yields
  no result (no in-view, no offer, no own-backlog dispatched), the leader must
  release leadership — not just when it dispatched from its own backlog.
- **No-cooldown-on-peer:** When the probe finds the offer list (coordination
  file) contains a peer with a dispatchable item, do NOT arm the
  `no-candidate` cooldown.
- **Documentation:** update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` to reflect the
  new "empty-leader step-down" contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — Worker loop
  that consumes `dispatchFromCoordination` outcomes; add step-down on
  empty-backlog; add peer-offer check before arming cooldown.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` —
  `dispatchFromCoordination` return value; may need to distinguish
  "empty-all" from "empty-own-but-peer-has-offers".
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — Offer list management;
  understand how peer entries are structured and dispatched.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — `releaseLeadership()` primitive
  (reuse, do not modify); verify idempotency.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — Dispatch filtering;
  understand the `no-candidate` exit path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — Tests for the new
  empty-leader step-down and no-cooldown-on-peer behaviour.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Document the new step-down trigger
  condition.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24** (completed) — Own-backlog fallback + step-down.
  Established the `ownBacklogDispatch` flag and step-down-on-dispatch contract.
  This item extends the step-down trigger to cover the empty-backlog case.
- **WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9** (completed) — Sprint-view-only dispatch.
  Established that the dispatcher no-ops when the view is empty; this item
  extends that to also step down leadership.
- **WL-0MTMPSCL8000O45H** — Coordination check-in / leader lease cadence.
- **WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7** — Probe before pause: the existing cooldown guard
  that this item extends to also check peer offers.
- **WL-0MUZPBSYW004I5D3** (completed) — Implementation of WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the seed description already carried a
clear problem statement, user stories, four measurable ACs, and live
production evidence. The questions below were resolved from code inspection
during intake.

- **Q: Where exactly does the step-down currently fire, and why doesn't the
  empty-backlog case trigger it?**
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** `dispatchFromCoordination` sets
  `ownBacklogDispatch: true` only `if (ownOutcome.dispatched)` —
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:874`. The worker
  loop calls `releaseLeadership()` only for that flag —
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:865-868`. An
  empty own backlog returns a non-`dispatched` outcome without the flag, so
  leadership is retained.

- **Q: Why does the empty leader starve peers for 60 minutes?**
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** The `no-candidate` branch probes the
  leader's own root only (`computeMostImportantItem(cfg.cwd …)`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:889`). When that
  probe finds nothing it sets `ctx.cooldownUntil = now + noCandidateCooldownMs`
  (default 60 min), during which the worker performs no polling — including no
  coordination-offer scan. Peer offers do not cancel the pause.

- **Q: Does the fix risk regressing the own-backlog-fallback hand-off
  (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24)?**
  **Answer (intake agent, AC precedence):** No — the existing
  `ownBacklogDispatch: true` step-down must be preserved unchanged; this item
  adds the *additional* empty-own-backlog trigger. Cycle outcomes that DID
  dispatch an in-view, offer, or own-backlog item must NOT step down (AC1).

- **Q: Is legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`) affected?**
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** No — `leaderManager` is only
  constructed when `coordinationDir` is set; legacy mode has no manager and
  `leaderState` is unconditionally `true`, so there is nothing to hand off.
  Legacy semantics are unchanged (AC4c).

- **Q: Should the leader still step down when no peer has an offer?**
  **Answer (intake agent, AC precedence / fairness intent):** Yes — leadership
  is a reward for having work; an idle leader must relinquish so a peer that
  wins the next election can lead. With no peer the same instance simply
  re-wins the normal election on a later tick (bounded by existing backoff),
  matching the A2 assumption of WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24. The peer-presence
  condition applies only to *not arming the cooldown* (AC2/AC3), not to the
  step-down itself.

- **Q: Is `releaseLeadership()` idempotent / fail-safe?**
  **Answer (intake agent, code evidence):** `releaseLeadership()` deletes the
  lock + lease files (`packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts`); re-invocation is
  a stateless file delete. The new trigger must still guard `exactly once per
  cycle` (AC1) and never crash (AC1 fail-safe).

# Extract sync types and git-exec primitives

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 2 of 6 — the bottom layer; every later child imports from it.

## Goal

As a maintainer of the sync module, I want the shared sync type declarations and
the git subprocess plumbing to live in their own small modules, so that merge
logic, identity checks and push code can depend on a stable leaf layer instead
of on a 1,867-line file.

## Context

`src/sync.ts` today declares 9 exported types interleaved with logic, plus four
git-execution helpers that every other concern calls. These are the only leaves
in the planned layering, so extracting them first makes every later child a pure
consumer with no back-edge into `sync.ts`. Lines involved (current numbering):
types at 82–147, 356–411, 1473–1509; git-exec at 26–100 (`sanitizeGitEnv`,
`gitExecAsync`, `execAsync`, `execGitCaptureStdout`, `escapeShellArg`).

Also fixes the one pre-existing cycle candidate: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts:2`
imports `type { MergeOptions }` from `'../sync.js'`; after this child it imports
from `'./types.js'`.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. `src/sync/types.ts` exports exactly `GitTarget`, `SyncResult`,
   `MergeOptions`, `IncomingCommit`, `SyncAllowedAuthors`,
   `AuthorIdentityOptions`, `AuthorIdentityViolation`, `AuthorIdentityResult`,
   `DeltaReplayResult` — moved verbatim (same members, same optionality, same
   doc comments), no additions or removals.
2. `src/sync/git-exec.ts` contains `sanitizeGitEnv`, `gitExecAsync`,
   `execAsync`, `execGitCaptureStdout` and `escapeShellArg` with unchanged
   signatures. All five are module-local in `src/sync.ts` today, so they may be
   exported *from `git-exec.ts`* for internal use, but none may be added to the
   `src/sync.ts` barrel.
3. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The 9 types are re-exported from `./sync/types.js` by the barrel; no consumer
   or test file is edited and the guard baseline is unchanged.
4. `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `MergeOptions` from `'./types.js'`; the
   guard's `TYPE_ONLY_BARREL_ALLOWLIST` entry for `merge-utils.ts` is removed.
5. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic; no module imports a module that imports it back.
   No runtime import of `'../sync.js'` exists from any file under `src/sync/`;
   the guard suite is green.
6. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes — including all 11 test files that import
   the barrel — with no test file modified, and `npm run build` succeeds.
8. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   `wc -l` for `src/sync.ts`, `src/sync/types.ts`, `src/sync/git-exec.ts` is
   recorded in the completion comment.

## Minimal implementation

1. Cut the 9 type declarations into `src/sync/types.ts` verbatim; import
   `GitTarget`/`SyncResult` from `../types.js` where the originals did.
   `MergeOptions` must live here (not in `merge-utils.ts`) — see parent plan.
2. Cut the 4 git helpers + `sanitizeGitEnv` into `src/sync/git-exec.ts`
   together with their imports from `../process-lifecycle.js` and `node:child_process`.
3. Replace the removed blocks in `src/sync.ts` with `export type { ... } from
   './sync/types.js'` (and a value import for internal use).
4. Re-point `src/sync/merge-utils.ts:2` to `'./types.js'`; drop the allowlist
   entry in the guard.
5. Build, run `/skill:test` (changed scope), record `wc -l` and both outcomes.

## Key Files

- `src/sync/types.ts` — new (9 exported types).
- `src/sync/git-exec.ts` — new (git invocation, env sanitisation, stdout capture).
- `src/sync.ts` — removes the type + git-exec blocks, re-exports types.
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — import re-point (only internal consumer).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — allowlist shrink (only test touched, and
  it is the guard created by child 1).

## Dependencies

Blocked by WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G (guard) — the guard must be green before the
first move so every later step is verified mechanically.

## Constraints

- Move-only: no logic edits, no signature changes, no renames of exported
  symbols, no new dependencies.
- Do not touch consumers (`src/database.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/api.ts`,
  `src/logging.ts`, `src/commands/*.ts`) or any test file.
- Land as one commit that builds green; `src/sync.ts` must never be left
  uncompilable between commits.

## Deliverables

`src/sync/types.ts`, `src/sync/git-exec.ts`, re-export wiring in `src/sync.ts`,
`merge-utils.ts` re-point, guard allowlist shrink, build + test evidence.

# Extract merge predicates, field-merge, merge and collateral modules

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 3 of 6 — the largest extraction; depends on child 2's
leaf layer.

## Goal

As a maintainer fixing a merge bug, I want the merge decision logic split into
predicates, the field-level same/different-timestamp merges, the public merge
entry point, and the collateral (comments / audit results / dependency edges)
merges, so that a fix to one of them does not require reading repo plumbing or
push code.

## Context

This is the densest region of `src/sync.ts` — roughly 900 of its 1,867 lines.
Current declaration ranges (plan-time numbering):

- predicates: `isRegressionDefault` 148–173, `isValueRegression` 174–192,
  `EMPTY_IS_MEANINGFUL_FIELDS` 190, `isEmptyMeaningfulField` 193–201,
  `isTerminalStage` 597–607, `isAttributedDelete` 608–611
- field merge: `indexItemsById` 222–229, `mergeRemoteItem` 230–286,
  `mergeSameTimestampItems` 612–880, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` 881–1179
- public entry: `mergeWorkItems` 202–221
- collateral: `mergeComments` 1180–1216, `mergeAuditResults` 1217–1256,
  `mergeDependencyEdges` 1257–1273

The predicate semantics are owned by WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ (assignee sync
regression guard) and `mergeAuditResults` semantics by WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS
(audit-fresh items must not be re-timestamped); both move unchanged.

**Cycle constraint (load-bearing):** `mergeRemoteItem` must live in
`field-merge.ts`, **not** in `merge.ts` — placing it in `merge.ts` creates
`merge → field-merge → merge`. `mergeWorkItems` (which calls `mergeRemoteItem`)
stays in `merge.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` holds `isRegressionDefault`,
   `isValueRegression`, `EMPTY_IS_MEANINGFUL_FIELDS`, `isEmptyMeaningfulField`,
   `isTerminalStage`, `isAttributedDelete`, moved verbatim. The barrel keeps
   re-exporting today's four public predicates (`isRegressionDefault`,
   `isValueRegression`, `isEmptyMeaningfulField`, `isTerminalStage`), while
   `EMPTY_IS_MEANINGFUL_FIELDS` and `isAttributedDelete` stay module-local.
2. `src/sync/field-merge.ts` holds `indexItemsById`, `mergeRemoteItem`,
   `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, moved verbatim,
   importing types from `./types.js` and primitives from `./merge-utils.js`.
3. `src/sync/merge.ts` holds only `mergeWorkItems`; it imports
   `mergeRemoteItem`/`indexItemsById` from `./field-merge.js` and must not be
   imported by `field-merge.ts`.
4. `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` holds `mergeComments`, `mergeAuditResults`,
   `mergeDependencyEdges`, moved verbatim.
5. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic; no module imports a module that imports it back.
   No runtime import of `'../sync.js'` from any `src/sync/` module; the guard
   suite and its cycle gate are green.
6. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   No consumer or test file is edited.
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts`, `tests/sync.test.ts`,
   `tests/sync-audit-results.test.ts` and `tests/unit/audit-sync-monotonic.test.ts`
   pass unmodified; `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes and `npm run build`
   succeeds.
8. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
9. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure is ≤ 1,000 lines.

# Extract author-identity, refs, prefix-filter and repo-context modules

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 4 of 6 — mid-layer; consumes child 2, feeds child 5.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the author-identity gate, the last-synced/remote ref
bookkeeping, the cross-project prefix filter and the repo-root resolution to
each live in a small, individually reviewable module, so identity-gate fixes
are not interleaved with git plumbing.

## Context

Four non-merge concerns occupy the middle of `src/sync.ts`. Current declaration
ranges (plan-time numbering):

- author identity: `normalizeEmail` 371, `isAllowAllAuthors` 376,
  `isEmailWhitelisted` 383, `getRemoteAuthorCommits` 412–449,
  `checkAuthorIdentity` 450–479, `buildIdentityRefusalMessage` 480–502,
  `getConfiguredUserEmail` 503–517, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` 568–596
- refs: `getLastSyncedRefPath` 518, `readLastSyncedRef` 527,
  `writeLastSyncedRef` 539, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha` 552–567,
  `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` 1358, `getRemoteTrackingRef` 1342,
  `fetchRemote` 1338, `refExists` 1360, `fetchTargetRef` 1369–1426
- prefix filter: `isOwnProjectItemId` 287–306, `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` 307–355

# Concurrent `/skill:implement finish` wiped `packages/shared` from the main checkout

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ (planning session, 2026-10-26)
**Type:** bug
**Priority rationale:** critical — the main checkout lost a whole package, and
the `wl` CLI itself stopped working (it resolves `@worklog/shared/worklog-paths`
from `packages/shared/dist`).

## Problem statement

While `/skill:plan WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ` was running in the main checkout
(`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, branch `dev`, HEAD `be2d7771`), every
tracked file under `packages/shared/` was **deleted from the working tree**, and
the (gitignored) `packages/shared/dist/` build output was removed as well.

Timeline (times UTC, 2026-10-26):

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| 13:16:09 | Concurrent session launched `/skill:implement finish WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF` in worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF-refactor-guard-database-split-invariants` (PID 2640027) |
| 13:16:40 | This session ran `wl sync` in the main checkout (succeeded) |
| 13:16:49 | `packages/shared/` directory mtime — all 25 tracked files gone |

Evidence:

- `git status --porcelain` reported exactly `25 D` entries, all under
  `packages/shared/` (`README.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`,
  `tsconfig.json` survived only as they were re-listed in the deletions;
  `src/database.ts`, `src/fields.ts`, `src/icons.ts`, `src/persistent-store.ts`,
  `src/lease-release.ts`, `src/model-cooldown.ts` and the rest were gone).
- `packages/shared/` (dir) mtime `2026-10-26 13:16:49`, matching the concurrent
  `implement.py finish` window; the parent `packages/` mtime was untouched
  (`2026-07-26`).
- `packages/shared/dist/` was absent (gitignored, so it does not appear in
  `git status`).
- After the deletion `wl` failed for every command:
  `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
  '/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/node_modules/@worklog/shared/worklog-paths'
  imported from '/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/worklog-paths.js'`.
- The concurrent `implement.py finish` log (`/tmp/guard-finish.log`) recorded
  `WARNING: Implement run_tests: IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND override is not
  subsettable — running full scope on
  .../wl-WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF-...`, i.e. that run escalated to full-scope test
  execution across the repo.

Nothing in this planning session wrote to `packages/shared/`; the planning work
only created work items, comments and a description update under
`.worklog/`.

## Impact

- A whole workspace package vanished from the developer checkout — silent,
  unreported, and only discovered because an unrelated command (`wl`) broke.
- `wl` — the single source of truth for all work tracking — is unusable while
  `packages/shared/dist` is missing, so work-item operations fail closed for
  every agent on the host.
- Any in-flight agent in the main checkout would have committed the deletions
  with `git commit -a`, silently reverting the package.
- A concurrent `implement.py finish` that was *expecting* a clean main checkout
  would instead have observed 25 unexpected deletions and could have aborted or
  mis-attributed them (the finish step "refuses if it detects changes outside
  the worktree").

## Recovery performed (this session, non-destructive)

1. Confirmed all 25 changes were pure deletions (`git status --porcelain` had no
   `M` entries) and that every path exists in `HEAD`.
2. `git checkout -- packages/shared` — restored all tracked files verbatim from
   `HEAD`; nothing was stashed, reset or discarded.
3. `npm run build:shared` — regenerated the gitignored `packages/shared/dist`
   so `wl` resolves again.
4. Verified `wl show WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ --json` succeeds and the work-item
   tree/comments are intact.

No work was lost, but the recovery was manual and outside any agent workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified and documented.** The exact code path in `implement.py finish` (or the subprocess it drives) that removed `packages/shared/` from the main checkout is named with file:line evidence, or, if unreproducible, the investigation records what was ruled out (concurrent `git worktree`, full-scope `run_tests.py`, `--no-refactor`, `commit -a`, `git clean`) and the residual hypothesis.
2. **Regression test.** An automated test fails if a command run inside a `.worklog/worktrees/<wl-…>` worktree deletes or modifies tracked files in the main checkout — reproducing the "main checkout mutated by a worktree-scoped run" defect class (the same invariant as [docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](../../docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)).
3. **Failure is loud.** Any agent step that observes tracked-file deletions in the main checkout while it was not the actor aborts with a clear error naming the paths and the actor, instead of continuing silently.
4. **`wl` resilience.** `wl` reports a clear diagnostic (rather than an `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack trace) when `packages/shared/dist` is missing, and suggests `npm run build:shared`.
5. **Concurrent-run detection.** `implement.py finish` refuses to start, or warns explicitly, when another agent process holds the main checkout on the same host (see also `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`).
6. Investigation notes and the fix are recorded as a comment on this item, and `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish/cleanup path under suspicion.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — any checkout-level git helpers.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — existing "don't mutate the live repo" guard; likely the right place for the new detection.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-scope escalation path.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` / `dist/worklog-paths.js` — `wl`'s `@worklog/shared/worklog-paths` resolution.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — dirty-main-checkout detection.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the invariant this incident violated.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing worktree-isolation guard; this item hardens it.
- Repository-boundary rule applies: the fix touches agent infrastructure under
  `skill/`, so it needs explicit authorisation before implementation.

## Open questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (for the agent-infrastructure owner):** should a worktree-scoped
  agent run be permitted to mutate the main checkout *at all* (current docs say
  no), or is there a legitimate cleanup path that must run against the main
  checkout? The answer decides whether the fix is "block" or "allow-list".
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the producer):** was `WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF`'s finish run
  aware it operated on a shared checkout? If a second concurrent finish run is
  likely, the detection in AC5 becomes the higher-priority half of this item.

## Problem

The test-run cache (`run_tests.py` + `test_cache.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- Editing only the contents of an already-modified file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group.
- A run's entry is queryable by `--summary` immediately afterwards from a clean checkout at the same HEAD.
- A cached result is visibly marked as cached in non-JSON output.
- Regression tests: (a) two runs with a content-only change between them do not share a cache entry; (b) `--summary` finds the entry written by the preceding `--scope full` run.
data.title: Test-run cache returns stale results when only the contents of already-modified files change

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to launch unattended work items
through the local proxy whenever the pool is genuinely idle, so a *fully idle*
machine does not sit silent while a dispatchable backlog exists.

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher defers every tick with reason `prefill-eta` on a
fully idle pool (`capacity_hint: idle`, `freeSlots: 2/2`, `prefillsInFlight: 0`,
`prefillGateWaiters: 0`, no owner lease, no running panes), because the proxy's
`queue_eta_seconds` (97.5 s) exceeds `prefill_budget_seconds` (60 s). On an idle
pool that projected wait is the *newcomer's own* cold prefill — an unavoidable
service cost, not a queue wait — and the estimate is uncalibrated
(`prefill_eta_samples: 1`, `prefill_eta_calibrated: false`, the proxy's
`MIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES = 5`). Deferring on it is a livelock: never dispatch ⇒
never calibrate ⇒ stay pessimistic ⇒ never dispatch.

## Users

- **Operator / pool owner** — "I left the machine free for hours; the backlog
  should drain instead of the dispatcher reporting `no-dispatch` forever."
- **Unattended agents (audit / implement / critical tiers)** — "I should be
  started whenever a slot is genuinely free, not gated on a self-inflicted
  prefill estimate."

## Evidence (`.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`, leader instance)

```
{"kind":"decision","operation":"no-dispatch","reason":"prefill-eta",
 "freeSlots":2,"totalSlots":2,"ownerPresent":false,"runningPanes":0,
 "contentionDepth":0,"capacityHint":"idle","prefillsInFlight":0,
 "prefillGateWaiters":0,"prefillBudgetSeconds":60,"queueEtaSeconds":97.5,
 "localIdleSeconds":1203.744,"localLastActivitySource":"startup", ...}
```

Reason histogram over the last 500 decisions: `prefill-eta` 51,
`idle-age-qualified` 34 (the transitional record immediately before the same
gate), `slots-unavailable` 6, `capacity-saturated` 5. The
`capacityHint: idle` / `freeSlots: 2` entries prove the block occurs while the
pool is genuinely free; the later `slots-unavailable` / `capacity-saturated`
entries are legitimate (a foreign-root audit occupies both slots).

## Root cause (verified in code)

1. `evaluatePrefillPacing` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts:284`)
   is called from `downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:514` — *before*
   candidate selection — and sets `deferReason = 'prefill-eta'` when
   `queue_eta_seconds > prefill_budget_seconds` (97.5 > 60). The defect is in
   that gate logic (feature `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`).
2. The proxy's `status_estimate()`
   (`llm-manager/proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ`) defines
   `queue_eta_seconds` as the newcomer's own prefill **plus** occupancy:
   `projected_wait_seconds(...).projected_seconds`. It also publishes the split
   terms `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds` and `queue_eta_busy_slots`, and the
   calibration flag `prefill_eta_calibrated`. With `busy == 0` the occupancy
   term is `0.0` and the whole ETA is the own-prefill cost.
3. Herdr's `parseLlamaStatus` (`downtime-worker.poller.ts:321`) consumes only
   `queue_eta_seconds`; it never reads `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds` or
   `prefill_eta_calibrated`, so the gate cannot distinguish "own unavoidable
   prefill" from "wait behind other prefills", and enforces an estimate the
   proxy itself refuses to act on while uncalibrated (the proxy's admission
   guard is inert: `_inert("insufficient_samples")` → admit).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Fail open while uncalibrated.** Given a proxy status with
   `prefill_eta_calibrated=false`, the dispatcher must not defer with
   `prefill-eta` on the published ETA — calibration is a prerequisite for
   pacing, mirroring the proxy admission guard's `insufficient_samples` inert
   behaviour. `prefill-cap` and `prefill-gate` deferrals are unchanged.
2. **Pace on occupancy only, never on the newcomer's own prefill.** Given a
   status with `busy_slots == 0` (no occupancy: `queue_eta_busy_slots == 0`,
   `prefills_in_flight == 0`), the dispatcher must not defer on the own-prefill
   term; any ETA-based deferral uses `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds` (the wait
   behind other prefills). The own-prefill term alone never blocks dispatch.
3. **Real occupancy still paces.** With busy slots whose occupancy ETA exceeds
   `prefill_budget_seconds`, `prefill-eta` deferral is retained with the
   existing reason string, no-candidate semantics, header token and decision
   record fields unchanged. The decision record additionally carries the new
   fields (`queueEtaOccupancySeconds`, `queueEtaBusySlots`,
   `prefillEtaCalibrated`) so a paced tick is diagnosable from the log.
4. **Backward compatibility.** On a proxy that does not publish the new fields
   (absent), behaviour is exactly today's, erring towards dispatch — an absent
   ETA/budget or absent calibration flag never blocks dispatch, and absent
   occupancy ETA is treated as zero occupancy (never as "unknown ⇒ defer").
   Malformed new fields are advisory (degrade to `undefined`), never reject an
   otherwise usable poll; the existing fail-closed gate counters
   (`local_prefills_in_flight`, `local_max_concurrent_prefills`,
   `prefill_gate_waiters`) keep failing closed.
5. **Tests.** New unit tests cover AC1 and AC2 (including the zero-occupancy,
   uncalibrated, `capacity_hint: idle` regression fixture reconstructed from the
   coordination-log evidence above), parser tests cover the new advisory fields
   (present / absent / malformed), and a tick-level test proves an idle-pool poll
   now selects a candidate. All existing `downtime-worker.*` and
   `coordination*` tests remain green.
6. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (prefill pacing section,
   status-field table) and `packages/herdr/README.md` (pacing bullets) describe
   the calibration prerequisite, occupancy-only pacing and the new evidence
   fields; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` no longer claims the own-prefill
   term defers dispatch.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Fix belongs in the herdr plugin (consumer misuse), **not** the proxy: the
  proxy publishes `queue_eta_seconds` exactly as documented ("wait a newcomer
  would face before its first byte", i.e. own + occupancy).
- Pacing must still only ever *reduce* concurrency: no raising the free-slot
  budget, no bypass of `slots_stale` / `slots: []` (`slots-unavailable`),
  `capacity_hint: "saturated"` (`capacity-saturated`) or the per-slot
  `lease_state` rule.
- No new configuration knob (a rollback switch is only added if the implementer
  documents why; ACs do not require settings surface). Pacing follows the
  proxy's own cap/budget/calibration so there is a single source of truth.
- Adding exports to `downtime-worker.ts` requires updating
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json`.

## Existing state

- `evaluatePrefillPacing` returns `{inFlight, cap, gateWaiters, budgetSeconds,
  queueEtaSeconds, maxSlotPrefillEtaSeconds, capacityBudget, deferReason}`;
  deferral precedence is gate waiters → cap saturated → ETA.
- The ETA branch tests `queue_eta_seconds > budget` **or** a per-slot
  `prefill_eta_seconds > budget`.
- `parseLlamaStatus` validates the three gate counters fail-closed and treats
  `queue_eta_seconds` / `prefill_budget_seconds` as advisory.
- Decision evidence (`downtime-worker.constants.ts`) records
  `prefillsInFlight`, `maxConcurrentPrefills`, `prefillGateWaiters`,
  `prefillBudgetSeconds`, `queueEtaSeconds`, `slotPrefillEtaSeconds`.
- The live proxy publishes `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds`,
  `queue_eta_busy_slots`, `prefill_eta_samples` and `prefill_eta_calibrated`,
  all currently ignored by herdr.

## Desired change

- Add the three advisory fields to `LlamaStatus` and parse them in
  `parseLlamaStatus` (`prefill_eta_calibrated` as an advisory boolean:
  malformed → `undefined`; the two occupancy numbers as advisory numbers).
- Extend `PrefillPacing` and `evaluatePrefillPacing`: skip the ETA deferral when
  `prefill_eta_calibrated === false`; use the occupancy ETA
  (`queue_eta_occupancy_seconds`, falling back to `queue_eta_seconds` only when
  occupancy fields are absent *and* occupancy evidence exists) for the queue
  term; keep the per-slot `prefill_eta_seconds` term only for slots that are
  actually busy (an idle pool has no in-flight slot ETA to respect).
- Record the new values in the decision evidence and add them to the kept
  decision-record shape.
- Update the two docs and the tests listed above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — add
  `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds`, `queue_eta_busy_slots`,
  `prefill_eta_calibrated` to `LlamaStatus`; extend `PrefillPacing` with the
  calibration/occupancy terms.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` — parse the new advisory
  fields (absent → `undefined`, malformed → `undefined`, never reject a poll).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — `evaluatePrefillPacing`: the
  calibration prerequisite and occupancy-only ETA deferral.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — new decision-evidence
  fields for diagnosability.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — gate call
  site (`:514`): confirm the corrected pacing flows into the tier budget
  unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` — AC1/AC2 unit tests
  (idle-uncalibrated, idle-zero-occupancy) alongside the existing pacing suite.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — new-field parse tests
  (present / absent / malformed).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — regression fixtures from
  the coordination-log evidence (idle, uncalibrated, 97.5 s queue ETA, 60 s
  budget).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.starvation.test.ts`
  — tick-level dispatch proof for the idle-uncalibrated poll.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` — export baseline if
  exports change.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — pacing
  contract documentation.

## Related work

- discovered-from: `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (Herdr downtime dispatch: pace dispatch
  to local prefill serialisation, completed) — the defect is in that feature's
  gate logic; this item is not a duplicate because that item's ACs are satisfied
  by the current (misfiring) gate.
- `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` (consume truthful per-slot capacity —
  `lease_state` / `capacity_hint` / prefill ETA, completed) — established the
  status-field consumption pattern followed here.
- `LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ` (proxy ETA publishing) and `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (guard /
  occupancy parity) — proxy side behaves as designed; this is consumer misuse.
- `LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J` (blocked review), `LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6` (open wedged
  prefill gate) — related but distinct failure modes (foreign-root occupancy vs
  a stuck gate), not fixed by this change.
- Automated related-work report: see the `## Related work (automated report)`
  section appended by the find-related skill.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (severity: critical, likelihood: high if unfixed):** unattended
  dispatch is starved machine-wide for every worklog root served by a herdr
  instance while the reference-prompt prefill estimate exceeds the admission
  budget — including fully idle machines.
- **Risk:** relaxing the ETA gate could dispatch into a genuinely contended
  pool. Mitigation: AC3 keeps occupancy-based pacing, and `prefill-cap` /
  `prefill-gate` / contention-depth gates are untouched.
- **Risk:** uncalibrated pacing is deliberately dropped, so a pool under real
  sustained occupancy will pace only after `MIN_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES` prefills
  are observed. Accepted: the proxy guard behaves identically (fail open), and
  `prefill-cap` still serialises prefills.
- **Risk (scope creep):** calibration-aware timeouts, a settings toggle, or
  proxy-side changes may look attractive — record them as separate work items,
  not scope.
- **Assumption:** the proxy keeps publishing `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds`,
  `queue_eta_busy_slots` and `prefill_eta_calibrated` with the semantics
  verified in `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py:status_estimate`;
  absence degrades to today's behaviour.
- **Assumption:** re-verification on the live host needs a genuinely idle
  window (a foreign-root audit currently occupies both slots, which is a
  legitimate `slots-unavailable` deferral).

## Open Questions

None. The seed context (incident log evidence, root-cause chain and draft ACs)
was sufficient to draft this brief without an interview.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which component owns the fix — the herdr dispatcher or the proxy's ETA
  publisher?** — Answer (seed context, incident author `Map`): the herdr plugin.
  The proxy publishes `queue_eta_seconds` exactly as documented (own prefill +
  occupancy, "wait a newcomer would face before its first byte"), so the
  consumer is misreading an intentional contract. Source: work-item description,
  "Notes / assumptions".
- **Q: Is calibration available as a signal the dispatcher can consume?** —
  Answer: yes. Research: `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
  (`status_estimate`) publishes `prefill_eta_calibrated` and
  `prefill_eta_samples` alongside the split terms
  `queue_eta_occupancy_seconds` / `queue_eta_busy_slots`; herdr's
  `parseLlamaStatus` currently ignores them. Source: `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
  lines ~884–915; `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` line ~321.
- **Q: Does the pool need pacing to remain safe when genuinely occupied?** —
  Answer: yes, keep it. `prefill-cap` (`inFlight >= cap`) and `prefill-gate`
  (`prefill_gate_waiters > 0`) stay unchanged and are the primary serialisation
  guards; only the own-prefill term is dropped. Source: existing
  `evaluatePrefillPacing` precedence in `downtime-worker.idle.ts`.
- **Q: Should a rollback switch be added?** — Answer (assumption, documented):
  no, unless the implementer finds one necessary; pacing follows the proxy's own
  cap/budget/calibration to avoid a second source of truth. Source: work-item
  description, "Notes / assumptions".
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the completed pacing feature
  (`WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`)?** — Answer: no. That item's ACs (cap budget, gate
  waiters, ETA deferral, docs, tests) are all satisfied by the current gate; this
  item changes the ETA deferral's preconditions. Duplicate check performed — no
  overlapping completed item covers the fail-open/occupancy-only behaviour.
  Source: `wl search "prefill eta pacing"`.
data.title: Prefill-ETA pacing gate defers on idle pool: uncalibrated/unoccupied own-prefill livelocks dispatch
