data.description:
# Downtime dispatcher starvation: three roots, three causes, one silent symptom

## Objective (headline)

Make downtime dispatch starvation **self-explanatory and non-permanent**: any root on this machine that has dispatchable work must either get dispatched, or report an exact machine-readable reason for not being dispatched — **never a bare `no-candidate`**.

## Problem statement

Diagnosed 2026-10-27T21:46–21:56Z: the downtime dispatcher reported `no-candidate` continuously while the GPU sat idle for ~7 minutes and three separate worklog roots each had dispatchable-looking work. Three **unrelated** faults collapsed into one **indistinguishable** log line:

| Root | Dispatchable in window | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `AI_Hell` (30-item window) | 0 | every item held by the producer sentinel `assignee=Map` |
| `tce-the-rising` (25-item window) | 1 (`in_review` → audit) | audit tier structurally unreachable at the default prefill cap |
| `ContextHub` (30-item window) | 9 | zero coordination entries — no live herdr instance in the root |

Leader decision log for the whole period: `{"operation":"no-dispatch","reason":"idle-age-qualified",...}` then `{"operation":"no-dispatch","reason":"no-candidate","freeSlots":2,"totalSlots":2,...}`. The AI_Hell instance (`87558ae9`) checked in every 5 minutes for hours writing `workItemId: null` **with no reason**.

### Root causes

1. **Audit tier unreachable at the default prefill cap.** `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` is evaluated against `effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget)` (`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:529-534`). With the default serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`, `in_flight: 0`, `freeSlots: 2`) → `capacityBudget=1` → `effectiveFreeSlots=1` → audit tier **never** eligible, so the `completed`/`in_review` queue never drains (AI_Hell: 1154 completed items; tce-the-rising: its single audit candidate has 0 dispatch-log entries).
2. **No attribution for empty offers or skipped tiers.** Check-ins log `workItemId: null` with no reason; the leader collapses every per-entry rejection into the terminal `no-candidate`; a tier skipped by the effective-budget clamp is invisible entirely.
3. **The `assignee` scheduling hold is invisible.** `assignee=Map` holds (AGENTS.md producer sentinel) are correctly refused by `classifyItemForDispatch` (WL-0MV85WCJJ0087VMP) — but an entire held window is indistinguishable from an empty or broken backlog.

## Users

- **Operator (primary)**: runs the local LLM fleet from herdr; the person who has to answer "why is nothing being dispatched?" — today it requires reading the dispatcher's source and re-running classification by hand. Wants starved roots to be self-diagnosing from the decision log and TUI.
- **Producer**: parks work with `assignee=Map` deliberately; wants the hold to be *surfaced* when it is the sole reason a root is idle, without the dispatcher ever auto-clearing it.
- **Audit-tier consumers**: `completed`/`in_review` items waiting on `/skill:audit` during downtime; currently starved under the default prefill configuration.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, I can read one line of `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` and know whether a root is empty, fully held by `assignee=Map`, fully gated, or paced — so I don't have to re-run classification by hand.
- As a producer, I am warned in the TUI when my own `assignee` hold is the sole reason a root cannot dispatch — so I can distinguish "I parked this on purpose" from "the dispatcher is broken".
- As an operator running the default proxy config, I can rely on audits draining the review queue during idle time — so the queue doesn't grow unbounded.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

- AC1: All three implementation children are `completed` and audited.
- AC2: A live verification on `AI_Hell`, `tce-the-rising` and `ContextHub` shows each root either dispatching or reporting an exact reason other than a bare `no-candidate`. **Accepted variance (producer decision, 2026-10-29):** `ContextHub` has no live downtime instance to observe — its `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` was last written 2026-10-27T00:52:43Z and the root-registry cause is out of scope in `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — so the recorded absence of an instance is accepted as that root's evidence instead of a forced dispatch (resolves OPEN QUESTION O2). The other two roots are verified live: `AI_Hell` dispatching (`AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O` check-ins at 2026-10-29T00:21:57Z and 00:27:04Z) and `tce-the-rising` reporting `all-window-items-gated` (00:19:48Z / 00:24:57Z / 00:30:07Z).
- AC3: No regression in the existing `packages/herdr` downtime-worker suites; the prefill pacing contract (WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX) still holds for single-pane tiers.
- AC4: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` reflects the final behaviour, including an explicit reversal of the documented audit-skip-at-cap-1 rule.
- AC5: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill and excluded).
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the canonical ranking contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head", WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).
- Do **not** widen the dispatch window (WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 stays in force).
- Do **not** raise the prefill budget above what the proxy reports, and do not change the default `local_max_concurrent_prefills` unless intake finds the audit tier genuinely needs concurrent prefills (it does not — see Intake record).
- Do **not** auto-clear `assignee` holds (A3).
- Root registry / sweep of roots with no live instance is **out of scope** — filed as `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y`.
- The `assignee`-hold surface must be strictly read-only and add no new `wl` subprocess spawns to the refresh path.
- Attribution tokens must be stable strings, additive-only (no change to dispatch decisions), and rate-limited like other decision-log entries.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:529-534` — `effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget)`; the value flows to the audit tier check (`downtime-worker.dispatch.ts:337`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:468`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts:344` — `capacityBudget = inFlight >= cap ? 0 : cap - inFlight`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts:84` — `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` documented as a slot-count requirement.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:957-968` — the silent `workItemId: null` check-in log line.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts:499-503` + `downtime-worker.selection.ts:72-86` — the silent `assignee` hold refusal (`isAssigneeHeld`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:290` — `recordDecision` already supports `blocking: false` observations with rate limiting (the mechanism AC3 of child 2 needs).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — currently *documents* the audit-skip-at-cap-1 rule as intended (must be reversed).

## Desired change

1. Evaluate the audit tier's free-slot minimum against the **slot budget** (`freeSlots`), never against the prefill-capacity budget; keep `effectiveFreeSlots` as the pacing input for single-pane tiers.
2. Record machine-readable empty-offer and tier-skip attribution in the decision log (`empty-window`, `all-window-items-held` + sentinel, `all-window-items-gated` + dominant gate, budget-skip tokens with the tier), plus per-entry rejection detail for coordination entries — additive only.
3. Surface an all-held dispatch window to the operator (TUI/worklist warning naming the sentinel values and count) with a shared classification helper used by both the TUI and the coordination-log token.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — effective-budget computation (`:529-534`) and decision-log writer (`recordDecision`, `:290`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — `evaluatePrefillPacing` / `capacityBudget` (`:344`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` (`:84`), decision-log constants
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — per-tier minimum checks (`:337`) and audit-tier selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — dispatch-time rejection path and check-in empty-offer log (`:957-968`)

# Intake Brief: client treats retryable "Local admission refused" 429 as a terminal error

## Problem statement

When the llm-proxy's prefill-ETA admission guard refuses local admission, a
request sent with `X-Local-Preference: local-only` receives an HTTP `429`
whose body is explicitly marked **retryable** and carries a server-computed
retry hint:

```json
{"error": "Local admission refused",
 "code": "local_admission_reject",
 "reason": "eta_exceeds_budget",
 "eta_prefill_seconds": 11.2, "budget_seconds": 60.0,
 "projected_wait_seconds": 74.4,
 "retryable": true, "retry_after": 15,
 "retry_at": "2026-10-28T15:45:39Z", ...}
```

with headers `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Admission: reject`,
`Retry-After: 15`.

The pi client (via the Worklog TUI extension's recovery module,
`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`) classifies this as a
**terminal** error and abandons the turn with a "Non-retryable error"
notification, even though the proxy told it to retry after 15 s.

### Evidence (2026-10-28 15:45:24, /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log)

Session `herdr-1793202136-1305210-5578` (model `plan`) sent a request with
`priority_routing ... preference=local-only` (line 80697). The guard refused
(line 80698):

```
local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget enforced=true
    eta_prefill_s=11.2 eta_occupancy_s=63.2 projected_wait_s=74.4
    budget_s=60.0 ... busy_slots=2 in_flight_prefills=1 free_slot=false
    session=herdr-1793202136-1305210-5578
```

`local-only` forbids remote fallback, so `provider._build_local_only_refusal_response`
(`proxy/proxy/provider.py:6506`) returned the 429 above with
`Retry-After: 15` (= `ceil(projected_wait - budget)`). The local model was
simply saturated (2/2 slots busy); 15 s later the same session was admitted
again normally. The refusal was transient and time-healable.

## Root cause

`classifyError()` in `error-patterns.ts` checks `isRateLimit()` (patterns:
`/\b429\b/`, `/rate\s*limit/i`, `/too\s*many\s*requests/i`) BEFORE
`isServerError()`. The 429 status code alone therefore wins, so the message
is categorised `RATE_LIMIT`, which `register-recovery.ts` treats as terminal:

```ts
case ErrorCategory.RATE_LIMIT: ... // Terminal: notify "Non-retryable error", stop
```

Proxy-side, this refusal is semantically *not* a rate limit: it is a
**capacity backpressure** signal that is (a) time-healable, (b) explicitly
flagged `retryable: true`, and (c) serviced with a `Retry-After` hint the
recovery loop is already built to honour (`resolveRetryDelay`,
`_lastServerRetryHintMs`, `retry_after` body parsing — the plumbing added for
WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI / the 503 startup-ramp gate). It only needs to be
classified onto a retryable path.

## Scope (what NOT to break)

1. **Plain 429 rate limits must stay terminal.** The fix must key off the
   local-admission refusal specifically (`error`/`code` prose
   `local_admission_reject` / "local admission refused"), not every 429.
2. **Non-retryable refusals must stay terminal.** The proxy also returns 429s
   with `"retryable": false` and no `Retry-After` for reasons waiting cannot
   heal (`prefill_budget_exceeded` — prompt above the 25 000-token admission
   budget — and `context_too_large`), with `suggested_action` = compaction
   guidance. Blindly retrying those would burn backoff time on a request that
   can never succeed without compaction. The classifier must discriminate on
   the body's `retryable` flag / `reason` field, not retry all 429s.
3. **Exhaustion-variant parity.** The same guard also surfaces as
   `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (`code: local_admission_reject`,
   error "All providers exhausted…") when the whole remote chain is exhausted;
   that message already hits the `EXHAUSTION_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS` / 503 path
   and is retried with the durable cooldown marker. Ensure the local-only
   refusal does not regress that path.

## Proposed direction (implementation options, not prescriptive)

- Add a specific classifier (e.g. `isRetryableLocalAdmissionRefusal`) checked
  before `isRateLimit` in `classifyError()`, matching the stable proxy prose
  (`local_admission_reject`, "local admission refused") plus the retryable
  signal, and route it through the existing SERVER_ERROR retry loop so
  `Retry-After` / `retry_after` are honoured.
- Keep `retryable:false` refusals (`prefill_budget_exceeded`,
  `context_too_large`) terminal, ideally surfacing the compaction guidance
  the proxy already sends (`suggested_action`) instead of a bare
  "Non-retryable error".
- Respect the bounded backoff/cooldown caps already in place
  (`DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG.cooldown` floor/ceiling,
  `max_retry_after_seconds: 3600` proxy-side bound) so an honest long
  `Retry-After` is honoured without pinning the pane.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Classification:** a message whose error text contains the local-admission
   refusal (`local_admission_reject` / "local admission refused") and a
   retryable signal (`"retryable": true` or `retry_after`) classifies to a
   retryable category (SERVER_ERROR or dedicated), never `RATE_LIMIT`.
   Covered by unit tests in `error-classification.test.ts` /
   `error-patterns.ts` tests.
2. **Retry behaviour:** the recovery loop retries such a refusal after the
   server hint (header `Retry-After` or body `retry_after`), bounded by the
   existing caps; it does **not** surface "Non-retryable error" and does not
   abort the turn. Integration test in `integration.test.ts` /
   `retry-loop.test.ts` style.
3. **Non-retryable polarity:** a refusal with `"retryable": false`
   (`prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large`) remains terminal and is
   not retried (no backoff burn), with the proxy's compaction guidance
   surfaced where available.
4. **No regressions:** plain 429 rate limits, 401/403, quota-exhausted and
   terminated messages still classify as in
   `error-classification.test.ts`; the existing 503 startup-ramp /
   exhaustion retry paths still pass.
5. **Docs:** `LOCAL_LLM.md` / recovery docs updated with the local-admission
   refusal semantics (retryable vs not) so operators understand what the 429
   means and that it self-heals.

## Notes

- Edge to verify: whether the extension reliably sees the JSON body in
  `errorMessage` (the 503 startup-ramp parsing in `retry-logic.ts` already
  consumes `retry_after` from message text, so the body is reachable; the
  fetch-wrapped `Retry-After` header capture is the fallback).
- Related history: WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI (Retry-After honouring for the 503
  startup ramp), WL-0MUVYA3VW008CH6I (adding a retryable pattern to
  `error-patterns.ts`), WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM (long Retry-After honouring).

# Clients: adopt `local-preferred` preference and honour the deferral contract

## Problem statement

The llm proxy is replacing the hard `X-Local-Preference: local-only` pin with `local-preferred` (llm epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY): a prompt that fits local capacity is kept local and *deferred* (retryable 429 + `Retry-After`, never remote), while a prompt that outgrows local capacity behaves as `remote-ok` and is served by the remote tiers.

The client-side plumbing shipped by this epic carries the new spelling end-to-end:

- `packages/herdr` (WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, complete): `LocalPreference` = `'local-preferred' | 'remote-ok'`, strict `isLocalPreference` gate, `clampDowntimeLocalPreference`, the `downtimeLocalPreference` setting, `--local-preference` pane-launch validation and the `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` forwarding.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference` (WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB, this epic): validates `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` before setting `X-Local-Preference` on every provider request.

Consequence observed 2026-10-28 (`herdr-1793209156-1928539-23885`): a downtime-dispatched `plan` pane pinned `local-only` was refused with a retryable 429 while its prompt comfortably fitted local capacity, and no cloud model was ever tried.

## Goal / users

- As an operator, I want to express "keep this local while it fits, otherwise let it go remote" once, in herdr settings, and have it reach the proxy verbatim.
- As an operator, deferred local-first work must actually resume once local capacity frees up.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 herdr accepts, clamps, persists, forwards and documents `local-preferred` end-to-end (`setting → --local-preference → HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE → X-Local-Preference`); the retired `local-only` is **not** an alias — it clamps to the fail-open default `remote-ok` (losing explicitness) and the migration note (`downtimeLocalPreference: local-preferred`) is documented.

- AC4 Deferral is end-to-end: a `local-preferred` pane hitting a busy local slot retries per `Retry-After` and completes locally, with zero remote dispatch.
- AC5 AC4 is not claimed until WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (pi client treats the retryable 429 as terminal) ships; the dependency is recorded in the epic's final comment.

## Children

- WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE (feature, **complete**) — herdr `LocalPreference` plumbing: `local-preferred` first-class, `local-only` retired (clamps to `remote-ok`). Covers AC1.
- WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB (feature) — Worklog pi extension emits `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, rejects the retired alias fail-open, records the forwarded value in the route log. Covers AC2.
- WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY (task) — end-to-end deferral verification (busy slot → `Retry-After` → local completion, zero remote dispatch). Covers AC4; blocked-by WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7.

AC3 and AC5 are cross-cutting and are satisfied by the children's own test/doc criteria plus the dependency edge recorded on WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY.

- Prerequisite for AC4: WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (retryable local-admission 429 treated as terminal by the pi client).

## Decision: `local-only` is retired, not aliased (2026-10-28)

Resolves the OPEN QUESTION on this epic (see intake comment WL-C0MVSNYRVL0011BIP).

- **Chosen: option B — drop the alias.** `local-only` is not accepted and is not

# Feature: herdr — adopt `local-preferred` in the LocalPreference plumbing (no `local-only` alias)

Parent: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (Clients: adopt `local-preferred` preference and honour the deferral contract).

## Problem statement

The llm proxy is replacing the hard `local-only` pin with `local-preferred` (llm epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY): a prompt that fits local capacity stays local and is *deferred* (retryable 429 + `Retry-After`, never remote), while a prompt that outgrows local capacity behaves as `remote-ok` and is served by the remote tiers. herdr still only knows the two old values (`local-only | remote-ok`) on every input surface — the `downtimeLocalPreference` setting, the derived explicitness flag, the `--local-preference` launcher flag and the `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` pane environment — so an operator cannot express "keep this local while it fits, otherwise go remote".

**Decision (operator, this session):** herdr adopts `local-preferred` as the *only* local value. `local-only` is **not** kept as a deprecated alias on any input surface — the plumbing exposes exactly `local-preferred | remote-ok`.

## Users and user stories

- **Downtime-dispatch operator.** "I want to set `downtimeLocalPreference: 'local-preferred'` once and have every dispatched pane carry that policy verbatim, so eligible work stays on the local model while it fits and only the genuinely oversized prompts go remote."
- **Producer / on-call engineer.** "I want the value that reached the pane to be greppable in one place (the dispatch marker and the normalised log line), so I can tell an explicit operator setting from the low-priority rule."
- **Operator upgrading an existing deployment.** "My settings file still says `local-only`; it is no longer a valid value, so I expect herdr to treat it like any other invalid value — warn/fail open to the safe default `remote-ok` rather than invent a preference or fail the launch — and I expect that loss of meaning to be written down, not silent."

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — `LocalPreference = 'local-only' | 'remote-ok'`; `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `isLocalPreference`, `clampDowntimeLocalPreference`, `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`, `BACKGROUND_LOCAL_PREFERENCE = 'remote-ok'`, `resolveDispatchLocalPreference` (`low` → `local-only`), `resolveDispatchLocalPreferenceDecision` (operator-setting > priority rule > deployment default), `LocalPreferenceMode`, `LocalPreferenceReason`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeLocalPreference` plus the derived, never-persisted `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit`; `loadSettings` clamps the value and derives explicitness via `isLocalPreference`, `saveSettings` strips the derived flag and keeps the key absent for non-explicit deployments.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — the only unvalidated-string entry point: a `case` statement forwards `local-only|remote-ok`, warns-and-drops anything else (fail-open), then exports `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — pushes `--local-preference <value>` and sets `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` in the pane env; `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` builds the dispatch config from the clamped setting; `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` applies `resolveDispatchLocalPreferenceDecision` and records `localPreference` + `localPreferenceReason` on the dispatch marker.
- Docs naming the values: `packages/herdr/README.md` (per-turn local-preference section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (locality-preference section and the dispatch-marker reason table).
- Tests naming the values: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` (forwarding contract), `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, plus `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- `LocalPreference` becomes `'local-preferred' | 'remote-ok'`; `VALID_PREFERENCES` and `isLocalPreference` carry exactly that alphabet. `local-only` is **not** accepted anywhere — no alias, no normaliser mapping it onto `local-preferred`.
- No adapter/normalisation helper is introduced: `isLocalPreference` remains the single strict validation gate, and `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` keeps clamping through it.
- `clampDowntimeLocalPreference` — `'local-preferred'` → `'local-preferred'`, `'remote-ok'` → `'remote-ok'`, anything absent/empty/invalid **including the retired `local-only`** → `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` (`remote-ok`).
- `resolveDispatchLocalPreference`'s `low`-priority rule emits `local-preferred`, keeping `reason: 'priority-low'`.
- `send-to-pi.sh` accepts `local-preferred|remote-ok` only, and warns-and-drops everything else (including `local-only`) while still exiting successfully; the exported `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` is therefore always `local-preferred` or `remote-ok`.
- Pane-launch and dispatch logging/markers record the clamped value, so a retired `local-only` setting is visible as `remote-ok` plus its `default`/fallback reason rather than as a silently mapped value.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` describe `local-preferred` as the value and state that `local-only` has been removed (rejected on read, clamped to `remote-ok`), with no back-compat alias.

## Constraints and decisions

- **Accepted values (input → effective):** `local-preferred` → `local-preferred`; `remote-ok` → `remote-ok`; absent/empty/anything else — **including `local-only`** → the fail-open default `remote-ok`. No new value is ever invented, and no retired value is silently reinterpreted.
- **No alias layer.** `local-only` is a removed value, not a deprecated alias: no `normaliseLocalPreference`-style helper, no `case` arm in `send-to-pi.sh`, no mapping in `settings.ts`. Removing the alias keeps one canonical alphabet and one validation gate.
- **Explicitness follows validity.** `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit` stays derived from `isLocalPreference` (unchanged code path). A settings file holding `local-only` therefore loads as `downtimeLocalPreference: 'remote-ok'` with `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit: false`, and a save round-trip leaves the key absent. This is the accepted behaviour change for legacy deployments (see Risks).
- **The `low`-priority rule emits the first-class value** (`local-preferred`) — the epic removes `local-only` as a first-class value, so no behaviour is lost.
- **Fail-open is unchanged:** invalid/absent values never fail a pane launch, never invent a preference, and never forward an unvalidated string.
- **No new dependencies and no behaviour change to `remote-ok`** — the default stays `remote-ok`.
- Out of scope: the proxy-side `local-preferred` semantics (llm epic), the client retry behaviour for the deferral 429 (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7), and the extension's header emission (sibling WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Alphabet, no alias.** `clampDowntimeLocalPreference('local-preferred') === 'local-preferred'`, `clampDowntimeLocalPreference('remote-ok') === 'remote-ok'`, `clampDowntimeLocalPreference('local-only') === 'remote-ok'` (retired value, treated as invalid — not mapped to `local-preferred`), and `undefined`/`''`/garbage all resolve to `'remote-ok'`; `isLocalPreference('local-only') === false`; unit tested in `local-preference.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — End-to-end forwarding.** A pane dispatched from a deployment whose setting is `local-preferred` receives `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred` and the launcher argv carries `--local-preference local-preferred`; a deployment whose setting is the retired `local-only` forwards `remote-ok` instead; both pinned by `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`.
- **AC3 — No legacy explicitness.** A settings file holding `local-only` loads with `downtimeLocalPreference === 'remote-ok'` and `downtimeLocalPreferenceExplicit === false`, and a save round-trip leaves `downtimeLocalPreference` absent (nothing is persisted for a non-explicit deployment); a settings file with `local-preferred` loads explicit with that value and round-trips unchanged.
- **AC4 — No unvalidated forwarding.** Every path that reaches the pane argv or env goes through `isLocalPreference`/`clampDowntimeLocalPreference`; `send-to-pi.sh` accepts only `local-preferred|remote-ok`, warns and drops any other value (including `local-only`), and still exits successfully.
- **AC5 — Tests.** `local-preference.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` cover `local-preferred`, the rejection of `local-only`, and the clamped wire value; no test or snapshot still asserts `local-only` as an accepted or forwarded value.
- **AC6 — Docs.** `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` present `local-preferred` as the supported value and state that `local-only` is removed and clamped to `remote-ok` (no alias); **all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts` — new alphabet, `low` rule emits `local-preferred`, retired `local-only` documented as invalid.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — no logic change expected (explicitness already derives from `isLocalPreference`); comments updated to note the retired value resolves to the fail-open default.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — `case`/usage/help accept only `local-preferred|remote-ok`; warning text names the valid values.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — forwarding of the clamped value (argv + env, log line).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — dispatch config from the clamped setting (no code change expected beyond comments).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — marker `localPreference` now records `local-preferred`.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — value tables and prose.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/local-preference.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- Parent epic WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (clients adopt `local-preferred`).
- Sibling WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB (Worklog pi extension emits `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`).
- Proxy-side contract, llm store: epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY and children LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (parser/alias), LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (capacity verdict), LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE (chain selection/deferral), LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z (test matrix), LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 (docs).
- Precedent in this store: WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (introduced the per-turn preference and route logging), WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 (flipped the downtime default to `remote-ok`), WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low-priority rule + derived explicitness flag), WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8 (parent plumbing: reservation + per-turn preference).
- Prerequisite for the epic's end-to-end deferral AC: WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (pi client treats the retryable local-admission 429 as terminal today) — not a blocker for this child, which only changes the value that reaches the wire.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — legacy `local-only` deployments change behaviour on upgrade.** With no alias, a persisted `local-only` becomes `remote-ok` and loses explicitness, so the low-priority rule applies again. Accepted by the operator as the intent of "no alias"; mitigated by (a) AC3 pinning the exact fail-open behaviour, (b) herdr never failing the launch, and (c) `packages/herdr/README.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documenting the migration step (rewrite the setting to `local-preferred`).
- **Risk — the proxy still accepts `local-only` for a release** (llm LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16). Accepted: herdr simply stops emitting it, so there is no cross-version incompatibility — only the one-way migration above.
- **Risk — missed literal in a test assertion.** `grep -rn 'local-only' packages/herdr/src packages/herdr/shared tests/herdr` enumerates the affected files; a full-suite run (AC7) is the backstop.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Aligning the *worklist/TUI help text* or the docs sweep across the whole `docs/` tree is out of scope for this child; anything beyond the two named docs is recorded as a follow-up work item rather than folded in.
- **Assumption:** the dispatch marker's `localPreference` field is consumed only by the route log and operator tooling, so changing the recorded literal does not break a consumer; verified by searching the marker field's readers during implementation.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Should `local-only` remain a deprecated input alias, normalised to `local-preferred`?
  — Answer (**operator decision, this session**): no. The plumbing exposes only `local-preferred | remote-ok`; `local-only` is treated as an invalid value and clamps to the fail-open default `remote-ok`. Consequence recorded in Constraints ("Explicitness follows validity") and Risks ("legacy `local-only` deployments change behaviour on upgrade"); AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 rewritten accordingly and the earlier alias-based ACs withdrawn.
- Q: Should the `low`-priority rule keep emitting `local-only` (now removed) or switch to `local-preferred`?
  — Answer (agent, from the epic's ACs): `local-preferred`. Rationale: the epic removes `local-only` as a first-class value, so the rule must emit the only remaining local value. Source: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 AC1.
- Q: Is the exact proxy behaviour for `local-preferred` verifiable from this repo?
  — Answer: no; the proxy contract lives in the llm store (LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY), which is not initialised in this environment. The wire value is the only client-side obligation, so the brief is limited to it. No OPEN QUESTION remains for this child.
## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0** – Clients: adopt local-preferred preference and honour the deferral contract (herdr + Worklog pi extension) (open)

# Feature: Worklog pi extension — emit `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred` (local-only retired)

**Headline:** Move the Worklog pi extension's local-preference alphabet to the proxy's new spelling (`local-preferred | remote-ok`), emit `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred` on every request, and treat the retired `local-only` as any other invalid value (fail-open: no header, no route log).

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy replaced the hard `X-Local-Preference: local-only` pin with `local-preferred` — a prompt that fits local capacity stays local and is *deferred* (retryable 429 + `Retry-After`, never a silent remote fallback), while a prompt that outgrows local capacity behaves as `remote-ok` and is served by the remote tiers.

The extension is the last hop before the wire and still speaks the retired dialect: its `LocalPreference` union and `VALID_PREFERENCES` are `'local-only' | 'remote-ok'`, so it can never emit the value the proxy's deferral contract keys off, and it forwards the retired spelling verbatim.

## Decision inherited from the parent epic (settled, do not re-litigate)

WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 records the decision: `local-only` is **retired, not aliased**. herdr already shipped that contract (WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, commit `2401d874`: `LocalPreference = 'local-preferred' | 'remote-ok'`, `isLocalPreference` as the single strict gate, `local-only` clamps to the fail-open default `remote-ok`). This item makes the extension consistent with the shipped sender rather than adding an alias layer the sender no longer produces.

## Users

- **As an operator** using a `local-preferred` pane, I want the extension to emit `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred` verbatim so the proxy applies the deferral contract instead of refusing the request.
- **As an operator** reading `.worklog/local-route.log`, I want the recorded `preference` to be the value actually sent, so route evidence is unambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `LocalPreference` is `'local-preferred' | 'remote-ok'` and `VALID_PREFERENCES` contains exactly those two values.
- **AC2** `resolveLocalPreference()` returns `'local-preferred'` for `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred` and `'remote-ok'` for `remote-ok`; it returns `undefined` for the retired `local-only` (no normalisation, no alias), for any other unknown value, and for an absent/empty variable.
- **AC3** `registerLocalPreference()` sets `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred` on `before_provider_headers` when the knob is `local-preferred`, and sets **no** header when the knob is absent, empty, `local-only` or otherwise invalid (fail-open preserved).
- **AC4** The route-log `preference` field records the forwarded value (`local-preferred` / `remote-ok`), and no route-log line is written when the knob is invalid/absent.
- **AC5** The knob is read per request, never cached (a re-launched or re-exported pane must never see a stale value); a broken hook still never throws into a turn.
- **AC6** `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` ("Per-turn Local Preference and Route Log") and the module docblock document `local-preferred` as the wire value, state that `local-only` is retired and fails open, and carry the migration note (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred`, i.e. herdr setting `downtimeLocalPreference: local-preferred`).
- **AC7** Tests cover: the new value, the retired value (no header, no route log), absent/empty env var (fail-open), an unknown value (no header), header casing, and the route-log `preference` value. The repo-wide test suite for the changed scope passes.

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts`
  - `export type LocalPreference = 'local-only' | 'remote-ok';`
  - `const VALID_PREFERENCES: readonly LocalPreference[] = ['local-only', 'remote-ok'];`
  - `resolveLocalPreference(env)` validates against `VALID_PREFERENCES` and returns the raw value.
  - `registerLocalPreference()` sets `event.headers[LOCAL_PREFERENCE_HEADER] = preference` per request and writes the route-log `preference` from the same value.
  - Module docblock still advertises `X-Local-Preference: local-only | remote-ok`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` — asserts the retired spelling end-to-end (including a locally declared `type LocalPreference` mirroring the union).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — "Per-turn Local Preference and Route Log" (≈ lines 476–503) documents `local-only` as the supported value and the `low` priority rule as producing `local-only`.

## Desired change

- Change the `LocalPreference` union and `VALID_PREFERENCES` to `'local-preferred' | 'remote-ok'`.
- Keep `resolveLocalPreference()` strict: an unrecognised value (including `local-only`) resolves to `undefined` → no header, no log. No alias, no normalisation layer.
- Update the module docblock, `index.ts` re-exports (no API change expected) and the README section (wire values, retired spelling, migration note, priority-rule wording).
- Update/extend the test file accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` — union, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `resolveLocalPreference()`, docblock
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` — value/retired/fail-open/casing/route-log tests
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` — export surface (likely unchanged)
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — "Per-turn Local Preference and Route Log" section

## Constraints and invariants

- **Fail-open is mandatory** (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ C4-AC3): unset/empty/invalid knob → no header, no route log; a broken hook never throws into a turn.
- **Read per request**, never cached.
- `remote-ok` behaviour is unchanged.
- No new dependency; no new polling loop.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the proxy already accepts `local-preferred` on the wire (llm epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY) — rollout is proxy-first, and the value is validated before it is emitted.
- **Risk (settings lag):** a pane launched by an older herdr forwards `local-only`; per the epic decision that now fails open (no header → proxy default), which is the intended migration behaviour, not a regression to fix with an alias. Documented in the README migration note.
- **Risk (test drift):** the test file declares its own `LocalPreference` type mirror; it must change with the union or the compile step fails.
- **Not in scope:** herdr docs/plumbing (`packages/herdr/**`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) — owned by WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE; end-to-end deferral evidence — WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY.

## Related work

- **Parent:** WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 — Clients: adopt `local-preferred` preference and honour the deferral contract
- **Sibling (complete):** WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE — herdr LocalPreference plumbing, `local-only` retired (commit `2401d874`)
- **Sibling (blocked):** WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY — end-to-end deferral verification
- **Prerequisite for the epic's AC4:** WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 — pi client treats the retryable local-admission 429 as terminal
- **Route-log origin:** WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ — Per-turn local preference and route logging (source of the fail-open invariant)
- **Default change history:** WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1 — Default downtime local preference should be `remote-ok`

# Task: end-to-end verification — `local-preferred` deferral (busy slot → `Retry-After` → local completion, zero remote dispatch)

Parent: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (Clients: adopt `local-preferred` preference and honour the deferral contract). This task covers that epic's **AC4**, which is deliberately separated from the two implementation children because it can only be proven after the retry-classification fix ships.

## Problem statement

The epic's two implementation children change what the clients *send* (`local-preferred` end-to-end). Nothing in them proves the behaviour the operator actually asked for: a `local-preferred` pane that finds the local slot busy is **deferred** — it receives a retryable 429 carrying `Retry-After`, waits, is admitted once capacity frees, and completes on the local model with **zero** remote dispatch. That chain also needs the pi client to stop treating the retryable 429 as terminal (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7), so it cannot be claimed by either child.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator who set `local-preferred`.** "I want proof that my local-first work actually stays local and resumes — not that it silently goes remote or abandons its turn after a 20-second wait."
- **Producer reviewing the epic.** "I want a single, auditable evidence trail (session ids, timestamps, proxy and route-log excerpts) so I can accept epic AC4 without re-running the experiment."
- **On-call engineer facing a deferred pane.** "I want the reproduction procedure documented, so the next time a pane sits idle waiting for capacity I can confirm it is deferral rather than a stall."

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- Deferral is refused today, not deferred: with `X-Local-Preference: local-only` the proxy returned a retryable 429 (`local_admission_reject`, `retry_after: 15`, `Retry-After: 15`) and the pi client treated it as terminal, abandoning the turn (observed 2026-10-28, session `herdr-1793202136-1305210-5578`; tracked as WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7).
- Evidence artefacts that already exist: the extension writes one bounded JSONL line per provider response to `<worklog-root>/.worklog/local-route.log` with `at`, `sessionId`, `preference`, `route`, `fallbackReason`, `model`, `ticket` (WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ); the proxy reports `X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`; herdr records the dispatch marker (including `localPreference` and `localPreferenceReason`). The proxy-side log path is host-specific and must be resolved at run time — it does **not** exist at `/var/log/llama-proxy/` on every host.
- Dispatch/reproduction entry points: `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh --local-preference <value>` for a hand-launched pane, and the downtime worker for a dispatched pane. Local-slot saturation is driven by concurrent local requests (the proxy's admission guard projects an ETA against a fixed budget).

## Desired change

- Produce and record the end-to-end evidence on this work item, then leave it ready for review. No production behaviour change is expected; if the evidence contradicts the contract, that mismatch becomes a **new** blocking bug work item (created as a child of the epic or a `discovered-from:<this-id>` item) rather than an inline fix.
- Document the reproduction procedure (how to saturate the local slot, which logs to read, what a deferred-then-admitted sequence looks like) so the evidence can be re-derived.

## Constraints and decisions

- **Blocked-by WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7.** Recorded as a `dep` edge (this item depends on that fix); the verification must not be attempted against a client that still classifies the retryable 429 as terminal, because a failure would be indistinguishable from the known bug.
- **No fabricated evidence.** Every claim must cite a concrete artefact: proxy log line, route-log JSONL line, or dispatch marker, with session id + timestamp. Synthetic fixtures may illustrate the expected shape but never substitute for a live observation.
- **Bounded, redacted excerpts.** Log excerpts recorded on the work item are trimmed to the relevant lines and must not include prompts, headers carrying credentials or full request bodies.
- **Evidence lives on the work item** (comments), not in a committed log file — `.worklog/local-route.log` is runtime state. If a doc change is justified it is limited to the deferral/reproduction paragraph in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **Zero remote dispatch is a hard criterion:** any `remote:*` route entry, or any fallback reason, for the verified pane means AC2 fails even if the turn eventually succeeded locally.
- Out of scope: changing the proxy's deferral policy (llm epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY), the client retry semantics themselves (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7), and herdr/extension value plumbing (WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE, WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions verified.** The item records that WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 is completed (its dep edge resolved) and that both plumbing children are in `in_review`/completed, together with the herdr and proxy versions used.
- **AC2 — Deferral observed.** A live evidence trail shows a `local-preferred` pane whose request was deferred by the proxy: the retryable 429 (`local_admission_reject` / `local admission refused`, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_after`) plus the client honouring the hint (a retry no earlier than the advertised delay) instead of abandoning the turn.
- **AC3 — Local completion, zero remote.** The same pane's turn completes on the local model, and its `.worklog/local-route.log` entries for that session show `preference: local-preferred` with a local route and **no** `remote:*` route or fallback reason.
- **AC4 — Auditable evidence recorded.** The work item carries the session id(s), timestamps, the proxy log excerpt and the route-log excerpt (bounded and redacted), and the dispatch marker's `localPreference`/`localPreferenceReason` for the pane.
- **AC5 — Reproduction documented.** The procedure to saturate the local slot and read the evidence is documented (in the item comment, and in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` if it is reusable operator guidance).
- **AC6 — Tests.** Any new deterministic test or fixture added for this work passes, and the extension/herdr suites covering the route log remain green; if no test is added, the item states why live evidence is the only viable proof.
- **AC7 — Docs.** **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC9 — Epic AC4 traceability.** Deferral is end-to-end: a `local-preferred` pane hitting a busy local slot retries per `Retry-After` and completes locally, with zero remote dispatch.
- **AC10 — Epic AC5 gate.** AC4 is not claimed until WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (pi client treats the retryable 429 as terminal) ships; the dependency is recorded on this item's `dep` edge and in the epic's final comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — deferral/reproduction guidance (only if reusable operator guidance is warranted).
- `.worklog/local-route.log` — read-only evidence source (not committed).
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — hand-launch entry point used to drive the reproduction.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` — route-log fields the evidence is read from (no change expected).
- Host proxy log — resolved at run time (path is deployment-specific; do not hard-code `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`).

## Related work

- Parent epic WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 (AC4 is the criterion this task exists to satisfy).
- **Blocking:** WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 — pi client currently treats the retryable local-admission 429 as terminal.
- Sibling children: WL-0MVSI1RX2005O9NE (herdr plumbing) and WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB (extension emits the header).
- Proxy-side contract, llm store: epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY; deferral/chain selection LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE; capacity verdict LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ; alias parser LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16.
- Precedent: WL-0MVLJTV03000KIQZ (route log introduced), WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8 (reservation + per-turn preference), WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI (the existing `Retry-After` honouring the deferral reuses).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — the verification window never appears naturally.** Saturation depends on real concurrent local traffic. *Mitigation:* drive it deterministically by issuing concurrent saturating local requests (documented in AC5) rather than waiting for an organic busy period.
- **Risk — evidence is ambiguous.** A turn that retried and then went remote would look "successful" but fail AC3. Mitigated by making the zero-remote criterion explicit and by citing the route log per session.
- **Risk — the proxy contract differs from the assumed shape** (`retryable: true` + `Retry-After`). If the live response shape differs, AC2 is re-scoped against the observed contract and the discrepancy is filed as a bug against the episode's proxy child rather than silently accepted.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Improving the recovery loop or adding new observability during verification is out of scope; findings become separate work items.
- **Assumption:** this host can reach the local proxy and read its log (path resolved at run time); if not, the verification is recorded as **blocked on environment access** with an explicit OPEN QUESTION rather than being marked complete.
- **Assumption:** route-log entries are keyed by pi session id, which is enough to attribute every request of the verified pane.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Why is epic AC4 not folded into one of the two implementation children?
  — Answer (agent): it depends on WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7 (client retry classification), which is outside both children's scope; keeping it separate lets the two plumbing children ship and close while AC4 stays honestly unclaimed. Source: WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0 AC4 text.
- Q: Should the evidence be committed to the repository?
  — Answer (agent): no — `.worklog/local-route.log` is bounded runtime state and may contain session metadata; the evidence is recorded as bounded, redacted excerpts in work-item comments. Source: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (route-log description).
- Q: Is a live run available in this environment right now?
  — Answer: unknown/not yet — `OPEN QUESTION` pending the dep edge resolving and the proxy log path being confirmed on this host. Not blocking this intake; it is AC1 of the task itself.

- **WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7** – pi client treats retryable local-admission 429 (Local admission refused) as terminal (open)
- **WL-0MVSI1S5P003UAMB** – Feature: Worklog pi extension — emit local-preferred, keep local-only as a legacy alias (open)
- **WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0** – Clients: adopt local-preferred preference and honour the deferral contract (herdr + Worklog pi extension) (open)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+347 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mvikrfp0005jdl8, 0mvljtv03000kiqz, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+342 more)

## Goal

Add one display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback: drop critical children from the top level and inject their root ancestor into the mandatory set, resolving parents in-process first with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback.

Parent: WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI. Core implementation feature; depends on the fetcher test feature and the root-filter feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback apply the same substitution before `selectWorkItems`.
- The critical subset is partitioned into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level).
- For each critical child, the root ancestor is resolved by walking `parentId` upward to the top-most non-child item; each resolved root not already in the merged candidate set joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`).
- Parent lookup uses the in-process SQLite fast path (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`) first, with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback; a per-refresh memo avoids repeat lookups.
- The substituted root is sorted by its own priority/group with no badge, marker, or indicator, and no stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage` is mutated.
- Fail-open: an unresolvable parent means the child is not shown; the refresh never crashes and never renders the child at top level.
- The `wl worklist` critical subset query and `wl list --priority critical` behaviour are unchanged (display-layer only), so the ship critical-items gate keeps seeing children.
- Drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children).
- No new hot-path `wl` spawn when the in-process path resolves (spawn-budget WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG not regressed).
- Stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with no synthetic/substituted rows.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`: add a shared helper (e.g. `substituteCriticalRoots(mandatory, candidates)`) that returns the mandatory list augmented with resolved root ancestors, and call it in `assembleDefaultWorklist` and in the `fetchNextItems` per-subset path before `selectWorkItems`.
- Resolve ancestors via the existing refresh scope / `withInProcessDb` read (`db.get`), falling back to `runWl(['show', id])`; memoise resolved ids per refresh.
- Keep `fetchChildrenForItem(s)`, `fetchItemsByStage` and `fetchItemsByPriority` unchanged.
- Do not mutate item fields; substitution is display-layer only.

## Constraints & risky assumptions

- No data mutation: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status` or `stage`.
- An ancestor may itself be a critical child? No — walk to the top-most non-child item.
- A substituted root resolved only via `wl show` may lack `childCount`; that is acceptable (AC: no badge/marker/indicator is added).
- Stage/priority-filtered views are exempt from substitution (they are explicit, already root-only filters).

## Dependencies

- WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI-F3 (fetcher tests) and WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI-F2 (root filter).

## Deliverables

- Updated `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.

# Bug: a retryable local-admission 429 is still terminal for the pi client (the refusal body never reaches the classifier)

`discovered-from:WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (end-to-end deferral verification) and
`discovered-from:WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (epic AC4). Found while verifying epic
AC4 on 2026-10-29 against the live llm-proxy.

## Problem statement

`WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7` ("pi client treats retryable local-admission 429 as
terminal", `completed`/`in_review`) added `isLocalAdmissionRefusal()` /
`isRetryableLocalAdmissionRefusal()` so that a *retryable* local-admission
refusal classifies as `SERVER_ERROR` and the retry loop honours `Retry-After`.

Live evidence (2026-10-29, proxy `192.168.0.199:8000`) shows the behaviour it
promised does **not** hold:

- the proxy defers a `local-preferred` request exactly as contracted —
  `429`, `code: local_admission_reject`, `verdict: deferrable`,
  `retryable: true`, `Retry-After: 62`, `X-Local-Route: refused`;
- the pane prints `Error: Non-retryable error: 429 "Local admission refused"`
  and **abandons the turn** — no wait, no retry, one request only in the proxy
  log.

Net effect: a deferred local-first pane still loses its turn. Epic AC4 cannot
be satisfied while this holds, and the operator-visible symptom is exactly the
one `WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7` was meant to remove.

## Root cause (verified, not inferred)

1. The proxy's refusal body carries the machine-readable fields as **siblings of
   a string `error` field**:
   `{"error": "Local admission refused", "code": "local_admission_reject",
   "reason": "...", "verdict": "deferrable", "retryable": true,
   "retry_after": 62, ...}`.
2. `openai/core/error.mjs` → `APIError.makeMessage(status, error, message)`
   prefers `error.message` and otherwise `JSON.stringify(error)`. With `error`
   a plain **string**, the rendered message is `429 "Local admission refused"`;
   `code`, `retryable`, `retry_after` and `verdict` are dropped (the SDK's
   `this.code = data?.['code']` is `undefined` for the same reason).
3. `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` →
   `isRetryableLocalAdmissionRefusal()` requires `retryable: true` **or** a
   `retry_after` / `Retry-After` hint **in the message text**. With neither
   present, `classifyError()` returns `ErrorCategory.TERMINATED` →
   `register-recovery.ts` notifies `Non-retryable error: ...` and stops.
4. The `Retry-After` **header** captured by
   `createRetryHintCapturingFetch()` only supplies the *delay* once a category
   is retryable; it never influences classification, so it cannot rescue this
   case.

The unit fixtures added by `WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7` pass because they feed a
message that already carries the JSON body; a real pi assistant message carries
only the SDK-rendered string. This is an integration gap between the proxy's
refusal shape and the client's classifier.

## Desired outcome

A `local-preferred` request refused by the proxy's admission guard with
`retryable: true` (or a `Retry-After` hint) is classified retryable **from the
response the client actually received**, so the turn waits the advertised delay
and resumes instead of being abandoned — with no cloud fallback and no
`Non-retryable error` notification. `retryable: false` refusals
(`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `context_too_large`, `resident_prefix_insufficient`)
stay terminal.

## Options (pick one at planning time; A preferred)

- **A — client-side (this repo, preferred).** Capture the refusal **body** in
  the existing `globalThis.fetch` wrapper that already captures the
  `Retry-After` header (`createRetryHintCapturingFetch()`), and let
  `isRetryableLocalAdmissionRefusal()` consult that captured body when the
  message text carries no polarity signal. Robust: it does not depend on how
  any SDK renders the message, and it is the same mechanism already trusted for
  the header.
- **B — proxy-side (llm store, follow-up, not a substitute).** Emit the refusal
  so the SDK message carries the fields — e.g. an `error` object with **no**
  string `message` (`{"error": {"code": ..., "retryable": true,
  "retry_after": N}}`) so `makeMessage` falls back to `JSON.stringify(error)`.
  Fragile (it depends on SDK message rendering) and lives in another repo, so
  it should accompany A, not replace it.
- Also worth fixing in the proxy (cosmetic, llm store): the refusal `detail`
  prose still reads `X-Local-Preference: local-only` even for a
  `local-preferred` request.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Classification from the wire.** A local-admission refusal whose
  `retryable: true` (or `retry_after` / `Retry-After`) is visible **only in the
  captured response** — i.e. the assistant message is exactly
  `429 "Local admission refused"` — classifies as `SERVER_ERROR` and the retry
  loop schedules a retry no earlier than the advertised delay.
- **AC2 — Non-retryable refusals stay terminal.** `retryable: false`
  (`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `context_too_large`, `resident_prefix_insufficient`)
  and a bare `429 "Local admission refused"` with **no** captured body stay
  terminal; plain `429` rate limits, `401/403`, quota-exhausted and terminated
  errors are unchanged.
- **AC3 — No stale-signal leakage.** The captured body is cleared on a 2xx and
  is scoped to the failing response (a later unrelated error must not inherit a
  previous refusal's polarity); pinned by test.
- **AC4 — Tests.** Deterministic tests cover AC1–AC3 through the public
  classification API (no source grepping); the existing recovery/extension
  suites stay green.
- **AC5 — Docs.** `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` ("Local-Admission
  Refusals (the 429 exception)") is corrected to state that the polarity is read
  from the captured response body, not only from the message text, and records
  why the SDK-rendered message is insufficient.
- **AC6 — Live re-verification.** Re-run the reproduction recorded on
  `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` and record: a deferred `local-preferred` pane waits the
  advertised `Retry-After`, retries, completes on the local model, and its
  route log shows `preference: local-preferred` + `route: local` with no
  `remote:*` entry.
- **AC7 — Full suite green** on the pushed commit.

## Evidence (bounded, redacted)

Pane `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred`, pi session
`01a18733-80c0-7794-bc9d-259169e02373`:

```text
2026-10-29 10:27:43,226 - INFO - priority_routing model=unknown priority=high
  providers=7 preference=local-preferred session=01a18733-80c0-7794-bc9d-259169e02373
2026-10-29 10:27:43,226 - INFO - Skipping provider=local-qwen3: local-qwen3 in
  cooldown (78s remaining) reason=local_provider_cooldown preference=local-preferred
2026-10-29 10:27:43,234 - INFO - local_only_refused reason=local_provider_cooldown
  preference=local-preferred verdict=deferrable
```

```text
Error: 429 "Local admission refused"
Error: Non-retryable error: 429 "Local admission refused"
```

Capacity-deferral wire shape (direct request, one local slot occupied):

```text
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-local-admission: reject
x-local-admission-eta: 40.6
x-local-admission-budget: 60.0
x-local-route: refused
x-local-fallback-reason: prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline
retry-after: 62
```

```json
{"error": "Local admission refused", "code": "local_admission_reject",
 "reason": "prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline", "verdict": "deferrable",
 "eta_prefill_seconds": 40.6, "budget_seconds": 60.0,
 "retryable": true, "retry_after": 62}
```

Full run notes: comment on `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.ts` (the
  `createRetryHintCapturingFetch()` wrapper) — capture the refusal body.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` —
  `isLocalAdmissionRefusal()` / `isRetryableLocalAdmissionRefusal()` polarity
  source.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — where
  the captured signal is installed and reset.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/*.test.ts` — AC1–AC3 tests.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — AC5.

## Related work

- Blocks `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (end-to-end deferral verification) and therefore
  epic `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` AC4.
- Regression of the outcome promised by `WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7`
  (`completed`/`in_review`) — the fix is correct for body-carrying messages but
  inert for the live wire shape.
- Proxy contract: llm epic `LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY`; refusal shape
  `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` / `LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ`.

## Risks and assumptions

- The refusal shape may change again proxy-side; A (capture the body) is
  resilient to that, B is not.
- Capturing a body in the fetch wrapper must not buffer streamed 2xx responses —
  capture only non-2xx, bounded (the existing header capture is already
  non-2xx-only and cleared on 2xx).
- Assumption: the same wrapper is installed before any provider request
  (`registerRecoveryModule` → `installFetchRetryHintCapture`).
